playbooks.title: Single-cylinder misfire
playbooks.summary: A misfire confined to one cylinder is caused by something unique to that cylinder: its coil or coil circuit, spark plug, injector or injector circuit, a local intake leak, or a mechanical fault such as a burnt valve, rings, a head gasket, or the valve train. Start with the freeze frame and misfire counters to learn when it misfires, then move the least invasive checks (coil swap, plug inspection, circuit tests) ahead of compression and leak-down testing. Confirm every fault before replacing parts, and address a flashing MIL promptly to protect the catalytic converter.
clarifyingQuestions: Which cylinder is misfiring, and has the MIL flashed?
Does the misfire occur at idle, under load, cold, hot, or all the time?
Any recent ignition, fuel, or engine work, or a recent car wash or heavy rain?
Is there coolant loss, oil in the plug wells, or a ticking noise?
What is the mileage and spark plug service history?

causes.title: Failed or weak ignition coil
causes.description: Internal breakdown or boot tracking prevents a strong spark on one cylinder, most often under load or in damp conditions.

causes.title: Worn, fouled, or damaged spark plug
causes.description: A worn electrode, wrong gap, cracked insulator, or fouling raises the voltage needed to fire and causes a misfire on that cylinder.

modifiers.reason: Plugs may be beyond their service interval

causes.title: Restricted, leaking, or inoperative fuel injector
causes.description: A clogged injector leans the cylinder; a leaking injector floods it. Either causes a misfire that stays on the same cylinder.

modifiers.reason: Injector circuit or balance code present
Symptom consistent with a leaking injector

causes.title: Ignition coil power, ground, or control circuit fault
causes.description: An open or high-resistance feed, ground, or driver circuit weakens or stops the coil firing.

causes.title: Injector control or supply circuit fault
causes.description: A damaged injector wire or connector stops or weakens injector operation on one cylinder.

causes.title: Low compression (worn or stuck rings, cylinder wall damage)
causes.description: Ring or cylinder wear lowers cylinder pressure, giving a steady misfire that is usually worst at idle.

causes.title: Burnt or poorly sealing valve
causes.description: A valve that does not seal leaks compression and usually causes a steady misfire and a rhythmic puff at the tailpipe.

causes.title: Head gasket leak into coolant or between cylinders
causes.description: A breached gasket lets compression escape and can let coolant into the cylinder, often misfiring worst on a cold start.

modifiers.reason: Coolant loss, white smoke, or overheating

causes.title: Valve train fault (worn cam lobe, collapsed lifter, broken spring, or rocker fault)
causes.description: A valve that does not open fully or close correctly reduces the charge or seal on one cylinder, often with a tick or clatter.

causes.title: Intake gasket or runner leak near one cylinder
causes.description: A leak at one runner leans only that cylinder, so the misfire is worst at idle and fades with load.

modifiers.reason: Lean code on the same bank

causes.title: Oil in the spark plug well (tube seal or valve cover gasket leak)
causes.description: Oil in the plug well degrades the coil boot and lets spark track to ground.

modifiers.reason: Oil leak around the plug wells

causes.title: Intake valve carbon deposits (direct-injection engines)
causes.description: Deposits on one intake valve disturb airflow and sealing, often causing a cold-start misfire.

tests.title: Review freeze frame, misfire counters, and fuel trims by bank
tests.purpose: Characterize when and where the misfire occurs so the following tests can be chosen.
procedure: Record all codes and the freeze frame for the misfire code before clearing anything.
Graph current misfire counters for each cylinder at warm idle, at a steady elevated speed, and during a moderate load road test where safe.
Record short-term and long-term fuel trims for each bank at idle and at cruise.
Note whether the misfire is worst at idle, only under load, only cold, or present in all conditions.
tools: Scan tool with misfire counters and Mode $06
tests.expected: Misfire confined to one cylinder with a clear operating pattern (at idle, under load, or constant).

outcomes.label: Misfire mainly under load or acceleration
outcomes.interpretation: Points toward ignition: inspect the plug and swap the coil first.

outcomes.label: Misfire mainly at idle with lean trims on that bank, improving with speed
outcomes.interpretation: Suggests a local air leak, restricted injector, or valve sealing problem; smoke test and check the injector.

outcomes.label: Steady misfire in all conditions or only on a cold start
outcomes.interpretation: A dead or constantly weak cylinder: check circuits, the injector, and compression.

outcomes.label: Misfire could not be reproduced
outcomes.interpretation: No change; operate the vehicle under the freeze frame conditions or review Mode $06 history.

tests.title: Swap the ignition coil with a neighboring cylinder
tests.purpose: Determine whether the misfire follows the coil.
procedure: Engine off: inspect the coil boot and plug well for oil, carbon tracking, or cracks before removing anything.
Swap the suspect coil with a coil on a cylinder that is not misfiring, noting both positions.
Clear the misfire data, then operate the engine under the conditions that produced the misfire.
Check which cylinder's misfire counter now increments.
tests.expected: Misfire stays on the original cylinder (coil not implicated).

outcomes.label: Misfire moved with the coil
outcomes.interpretation: The coil is at fault; inspect the plug well for oil that may have damaged the boot.

outcomes.label: Misfire stayed on the original cylinder
outcomes.interpretation: The coil is unlikely; continue with the plug, injector, and compression.

outcomes.label: Misfire did not reappear during the test
outcomes.interpretation: No change; repeat under the freeze frame conditions.

tests.title: Remove and inspect the spark plug from the misfiring cylinder
tests.purpose: Read the plug condition for ignition wear or signs of fuel, oil, or coolant entering the cylinder.
procedure: Allow the engine to cool, blow debris from the plug well, and remove the coil and plug.
Check the plug type, electrode wear, and gap against service information.
Look for cracked insulators, carbon tracking, and fuel, oil, or coolant deposits; compare with a plug from a good cylinder.
Check the plug well for oil or water.
Reinstall plugs tightened to the OEM specification.
tools: Spark plug socket and torque wrench
tests.expected: Plug of the correct type, within service condition and gap, and similar in appearance to plugs from good cylinders.

outcomes.label: Plug looks like the good cylinders
outcomes.interpretation: The plug is not the cause; continue with the coil, injector, and compression.

outcomes.label: Plug worn, gapped wide, cracked, or tracked
outcomes.interpretation: Replace plugs as a set; a tracked insulator may also have damaged the coil boot.

outcomes.label: Oil in the plug well or oil fouling on the plug
outcomes.interpretation: Oil in the well points to a tube seal leak; oil fouling on the firing end points to rings or valve guides.

outcomes.label: Plug steam-cleaned, coolant crusted, or fuel-soaked
outcomes.interpretation: Coolant signs point to a head gasket; fuel soaking points to a leaking injector or a cylinder that is not firing.

outcomes.label: Plug not accessible without extensive disassembly
outcomes.interpretation: No change; use other tests first.

tests.title: Test coil power, ground, and control on the misfiring cylinder
tests.purpose: Confirm the coil receives proper supply, ground, and a trigger signal from the PCM.
procedure: Back-probe the coil connector without piercing the insulation.
With the engine running or cranking, measure voltage drop on the supply and ground circuits against the battery.
Scope the control (trigger) signal and compare it with a good cylinder.
Where accessible, scope the primary current ramp and compare with a good coil.
Wiggle the harness while monitoring for dropouts.
tests.expected: Supply and ground within the allowable voltage drop and a trigger signal matching the good cylinders (limits per OEM specification).

outcomes.label: Supply, ground, and trigger all good
outcomes.interpretation: The circuit is not at fault.

outcomes.label: Excessive voltage drop, missing trigger, or intermittent dropout
outcomes.interpretation: Repair the wiring, connector, or feed; confirm PCM driver operation only after the wiring is proven good.

outcomes.label: Circuits good but the coil's primary current ramp is abnormal
outcomes.interpretation: An internal coil fault; confirm with a coil swap.

outcomes.label: Unable to access the coil connector safely
outcomes.interpretation: No change; use the coil swap test instead.

tests.title: Test the injector and its circuit on the misfiring cylinder
tests.purpose: Confirm whether the injector is being driven correctly and delivering fuel like the others.
procedure: Scope the injector control signal and supply voltage, comparing with a good cylinder.
Measure injector current with a low-amp probe and compare the pintle signature with the other injectors.
Port injection: perform an injector balance (pressure drop) test per the OEM procedure with fire precautions in place.
Direct injection: use the OEM cylinder contribution or injector tests; do not open the high-pressure system.
Optionally swap the injector with a neighbor where the design allows and see if the misfire follows.
tools: Fuel pressure gauge and injector pulser (port injection)
tests.expected: Injector signal, current, and flow match the other cylinders (variation limits per OEM specification).

outcomes.label: Injector control and flow match the others
outcomes.interpretation: The injector and its circuit are not the cause.

outcomes.label: Signal present but abnormal pintle signature, low flow, or leakage
outcomes.interpretation: Service or replace the injector per the OEM procedure and recheck misfire counters.

outcomes.label: Missing supply, missing or distorted control signal
outcomes.interpretation: Trace the injector wiring and connector before considering the PCM driver.

outcomes.label: Test could not be completed on this injection system
outcomes.interpretation: No change; rely on cylinder contribution data and other tests.

tests.title: Relative and cranking compression test
tests.purpose: Confirm or rule out a mechanical cause on the misfiring cylinder.
procedure: Disable fuel and ignition per the OEM procedure.
Perform a relative compression test using a lab scope and high-amp probe on the starter cable.
Perform a cranking compression test on the suspect cylinder and at least one good cylinder.
Compare values with each other and with the OEM specification.
tests.expected: Compression even across cylinders and within the OEM specification.

outcomes.label: Compression even and within specification
outcomes.interpretation: Major sealing problems are unlikely; valve train and deposits remain possible.

outcomes.label: Suspect cylinder low
outcomes.interpretation: Perform a leak-down test to find where compression is escaping.

outcomes.label: Two adjacent cylinders low
outcomes.interpretation: Strongly suggests a head gasket breach between cylinders.

outcomes.label: Could not safely disable fuel and ignition
outcomes.interpretation: No change; consult the OEM procedure before repeating.

tests.title: Cylinder leak-down test on the low cylinder
tests.purpose: Locate where compression escapes once a cylinder is confirmed low.
procedure: Warm engine off. Bring the suspect piston to top dead center on the compression stroke and hold the crankshaft so it cannot rotate.
Pressurize the cylinder with regulated shop air through the leak-down tester.
Listen at the throttle body (intake valve), tailpipe (exhaust valve), oil fill (rings), and watch the coolant reservoir for bubbles (head gasket) with the cap removed only when cool.
Record percentage leakage and compare with a good cylinder.
tests.expected: Leakage low and similar to good cylinders (acceptable leakage per OEM specification or tester guidance (general guideline — verify against OEM specification)).

outcomes.label: Leakage low even though compression is low
outcomes.interpretation: Valves and rings seal when closed: suspect a valve that is not opening fully (cam lobe, lifter, rocker).

outcomes.label: Air escapes at the throttle body or tailpipe
outcomes.interpretation: A valve is not sealing (burnt valve, bent valve, or valve held open).

outcomes.label: Air escapes at the oil fill
outcomes.interpretation: Ring or cylinder wall sealing problem.

outcomes.label: Bubbles in the coolant or air from an adjacent spark plug hole
outcomes.interpretation: Head gasket breach or cracked head; confirm with a combustion gas test.

outcomes.label: Compression was normal; leak-down not performed
outcomes.interpretation: No change.

tests.title: Smoke test the intake runners and gaskets
tests.purpose: Find a localized air leak near the misfiring cylinder.
procedure: Engine off. Seal the intake at the air filter or MAF outlet according to the smoke machine instructions.
Introduce smoke and inspect the intake gasket at each runner, injector O-rings, and nearby vacuum hoses with a bright light.
Pay particular attention to the runner feeding the misfiring cylinder.
Remove the equipment and reconnect all hoses.
tests.expected: No smoke escapes near the misfiring cylinder or elsewhere.

outcomes.label: No smoke escapes
outcomes.interpretation: A localized intake leak is unlikely.

outcomes.label: Smoke at the runner or injector seal for the misfiring cylinder
outcomes.interpretation: Repair the leak and recheck misfire counters and trims.

outcomes.label: Smoke elsewhere in the intake, away from the misfiring cylinder
outcomes.interpretation: Repair it, but it probably does not explain a single-cylinder misfire.

outcomes.label: Could not seal the intake for testing
outcomes.interpretation: No change; try propane or a spray enrichment check with fire precautions.

tests.title: Check valve operation on the misfiring cylinder
tests.purpose: Identify a worn lobe, collapsed lifter, or broken spring when compression and leak-down do not explain the misfire.
procedure: Perform a running compression or in-cylinder pressure waveform on the suspect cylinder where equipment allows and compare the exhaust and intake pulses with a good cylinder.
Alternatively, remove the valve cover per the OEM procedure and rotate the engine by hand, watching the rocker or follower movement on each valve.
Check for broken or weak valve springs, loose rockers, and visible cam lobe wear.
Reinstall with a new gasket as required and tighten to the OEM specification.
tools: Pressure transducer and lab scope (running compression)
Hand tools and new valve cover gasket (visual check)
tests.expected: All valves on the suspect cylinder open and close like those on a good cylinder.

outcomes.label: Valve movement matches the good cylinders
outcomes.interpretation: Valve train is not the cause.

outcomes.label: Reduced lift, collapsed lifter, loose rocker, or broken spring found
outcomes.interpretation: Repair the valve train and investigate lubrication before the engine is returned to service.

outcomes.label: Test deferred due to access or equipment
outcomes.interpretation: No change.

tests.title: Borescope the intake valve on the misfiring cylinder
tests.purpose: Confirm intake valve deposits on direct-injection engines before recommending cleaning.
procedure: With the engine cool, gain access to the intake port per the OEM procedure.
Rotate the engine by hand so the intake valve is closed.
Inspect the valve and port with a borescope and compare with other cylinders.
tests.expected: Only light, even deposits on the intake valves.

outcomes.label: Light or normal deposits
outcomes.interpretation: Deposits are not the cause.

outcomes.label: Heavy carbon on the suspect cylinder's intake valve
outcomes.interpretation: Clean the valves by an OEM-approved method and check bulletins for causes such as PCV oil carryover.

outcomes.label: Could not access the port
outcomes.interpretation: No change.

verification: Clear codes after recording the freeze frame.
Operate the vehicle under the conditions that set the code, including a cold start if applicable.
Confirm misfire counters for all cylinders stay at or near zero and Mode $06 misfire results pass.
Confirm no misfire or related codes return after a full drive cycle.

playbooks.title: Random or multiple-cylinder misfire
playbooks.summary: A random misfire (P0300) or misfire on several cylinders points to something shared by all cylinders: a lean condition from intake leaks, low fuel supply, or an under-reporting MAF; low ignition energy from worn plugs or a shared coil feed; poor fuel; EGR flow at idle; retarded valve timing; or general mechanical wear. Fuel trims and the misfire pattern decide which branch to follow. A noisy crank signal can also cause false misfire counts. Confirm the cause before replacing parts, and treat a flashing MIL as urgent to protect the catalytic converter.
clarifyingQuestions: Are fuel trims positive (lean) on one or both banks?
Does the misfire occur at idle, under load, cold, or after refueling?
When were the spark plugs last replaced?
Any lean, EGR, fuel pressure, or cam/crank correlation codes with the P0300?
Is there a start-up rattle, oil consumption, or a hissing noise?

causes.title: Vacuum leak (unmetered air)
causes.description: Unmetered air leans every cylinder, and the leanest cylinders misfire first, mainly at idle and light load.

modifiers.reason: Hoses and gaskets harden with age

causes.title: PCV valve stuck open or PCV hose leak
causes.description: Excess crankcase ventilation flow or a split PCV hose adds unmetered air to all cylinders.

causes.title: Low fuel pressure or volume (pump, filter, or regulator)
causes.description: Insufficient fuel supply leans all cylinders, most noticeably under load and at higher speed.

modifiers.reason: Fuel pressure or pump code present

causes.title: Worn or fouled spark plugs (set)
causes.description: Plugs worn beyond their interval need higher firing voltage in every cylinder, causing random misfire under load.

modifiers.reason: Plugs may be beyond their service interval
Misfire under load or in damp conditions

causes.title: Shared ignition coil power or ground circuit fault
causes.description: A weak feed or ground common to several coils reduces spark energy on multiple cylinders.

causes.title: Contaminated or incorrect fuel
causes.description: Water, debris, or the wrong fuel affects every cylinder, often starting right after a fill-up.

causes.title: Contaminated or under-reporting mass airflow sensor
causes.description: An under-reporting MAF causes under-fueling across all cylinders, most noticeably under load.

modifiers.reason: Aftermarket or recently serviced air filter

causes.title: EGR valve flowing when it should be closed
causes.description: Exhaust gas admitted at idle or light load dilutes the charge and causes misfire across several cylinders.

causes.title: Stretched timing chain or worn guides
causes.description: Retarded valve timing lowers cylinder filling and effective compression across all cylinders.

causes.title: Crankshaft position signal fault (false misfire detection)
causes.description: A noisy or erratic crank signal can make the PCM count misfires that are not occurring, or cause real misfires if timing is disturbed.

modifiers.reason: Misfire counted while the engine seems smooth

causes.title: Low compression on several cylinders
causes.description: General ring or valve wear across cylinders produces random misfire, usually with oil consumption or low power.

causes.title: Intake valve carbon deposits (direct-injection engines)
causes.description: Deposits on several intake valves disturb airflow and sealing, producing random misfire that is worst cold.

tests.title: Review freeze frame, misfire distribution, and fuel trims
tests.purpose: Decide whether the random misfire is lean-driven, ignition-driven, or tied to idle and cold operation.
procedure: Record codes and the freeze frame (load, rpm, ECT, trims) before clearing.
Graph misfire counters for all cylinders at idle, at a steady elevated speed, and under moderate load where safe.
Record short-term and long-term fuel trims per bank at idle and at cruise.
Note whether misfire is spread across cylinders on one bank or both, and when it occurs.
tools: Scan tool with misfire counters and Mode $06
tests.expected: Fuel trims near zero (general guideline: total within roughly ±10% (general guideline — verify against OEM specification)) with misfire pattern identified.

outcomes.label: Misfire with high positive fuel trims
outcomes.interpretation: Find the lean cause first: intake leak, fuel supply, or MAF.

outcomes.label: Normal trims; misfire mainly under load or acceleration
outcomes.interpretation: Points toward ignition energy, fuel quality, or a crank signal issue.

outcomes.label: Normal trims; misfire mainly at idle or when cold
outcomes.interpretation: Check EGR at idle, valve timing, compression, and intake valve deposits.

outcomes.label: Misfire could not be reproduced
outcomes.interpretation: No change; drive under the freeze frame conditions or review Mode $06 history.

tests.title: Smoke test the intake and PCV system
tests.purpose: Locate unmetered air that leans all cylinders.
procedure: Engine off. Seal the intake at the air filter or MAF outlet per the smoke machine instructions.
Introduce smoke and inspect vacuum hoses, intake and throttle body gaskets, brake booster hose, PCV valve and hoses, oil fill cap, and dipstick seal.
Remove the equipment and reconnect all hoses.
tests.expected: No smoke escapes from the intake or PCV system.

outcomes.label: No smoke escapes
outcomes.interpretation: No significant intake leak.

outcomes.label: Smoke at a vacuum hose, gasket, or intake component
outcomes.interpretation: Repair the leak, then recheck trims and misfire counters.

outcomes.label: Smoke at the PCV valve, PCV hoses, oil cap, or dipstick seal
outcomes.interpretation: Repair the PCV leak or replace the stuck valve and recheck.

outcomes.label: Could not seal the intake
outcomes.interpretation: No change; use propane enrichment or other leak checks with fire precautions.

tests.title: Check fuel pressure and volume under load
tests.purpose: Confirm the fuel system keeps up with demand when the misfire occurs.
procedure: Connect a fuel pressure gauge (port injection) or monitor the low-side and rail pressure PIDs (direct injection) per the OEM procedure.
Record pressure at idle, then during a snap and a loaded road test with a helper watching the gauge or data.
Compare actual with desired pressure and with the OEM specification.
Check for fuel leaks at the gauge connection before and after the test.
tests.expected: Fuel pressure stays within the OEM specification and tracks desired pressure under load.

outcomes.label: Pressure holds under load
outcomes.interpretation: Fuel supply is adequate.

outcomes.label: Pressure falls below specification or desired under load
outcomes.interpretation: Diagnose the supply: pump, filter, regulator, and pump circuit.

outcomes.label: Could not connect a gauge or no pressure PID available
outcomes.interpretation: No change.

tests.title: Check MAF plausibility and inspect the sensing element
tests.purpose: Determine whether the MAF is under-reporting airflow.
procedure: At warm idle, compare MAF airflow with the expected value (general guideline: roughly equal in grams per second to engine displacement in liters (general guideline — verify against OEM specification)).
During a safe wide-open-throttle acceleration, record peak MAF and compare with expected airflow for the engine.
Compare calculated load with expected values and with the other sensors.
Key off: inspect the MAF element for oil, dust, or damage and check the air filter and duct for leaks after the sensor.
tests.expected: MAF readings plausible for the engine and element clean (values per OEM specification).

outcomes.label: MAF readings plausible and element clean
outcomes.interpretation: The MAF is not the cause.

outcomes.label: MAF reads low or the element is contaminated
outcomes.interpretation: Clean with MAF-safe cleaner if the OEM allows, fix the filter or duct cause, and retest before replacing.

outcomes.label: Could not perform the loaded test safely
outcomes.interpretation: No change; use idle data and the visual check.

tests.title: Remove and inspect all spark plugs
tests.purpose: Look for worn plugs or a fouling pattern shared by every cylinder.
procedure: Let the engine cool, clean around the plug wells, and remove all plugs, keeping them in cylinder order.
Check type, gap, and electrode wear against service information.
Look for deposits common to all plugs (carbon, oil, fuel additives) and for cracked insulators.
Reinstall or replace, tightening to the OEM specification.
tools: Spark plug socket and torque wrench
tests.expected: Plugs of the correct type and in serviceable condition with a normal appearance.

outcomes.label: Plugs in good condition
outcomes.interpretation: Plugs are not the cause.

outcomes.label: Plugs worn, wrong type, or gapped wide
outcomes.interpretation: Replace the plugs as a set and recheck.

outcomes.label: All plugs fouled with carbon, oil, or unusual deposits
outcomes.interpretation: Fouling is a result; find the cause (fuel quality, oil consumption, or rich running).

outcomes.label: Plugs not accessible without major disassembly
outcomes.interpretation: No change.

tests.title: Voltage drop test on the shared coil supply and ground
tests.purpose: Find a weak feed or ground common to several coils.
procedure: Identify the shared coil supply fuse or relay and ground points from the wiring diagram.
Back-probe a coil connector and measure supply and ground voltage drop against the battery while cranking and while running under load.
Scope the supply while the engine runs and look for dips that coincide with the misfire.
Inspect shared grounds and connectors for corrosion or looseness.
tests.expected: Supply and ground voltage drop within the OEM limit with no dips while running.

outcomes.label: Supply and ground good
outcomes.interpretation: The shared circuit is not the cause.

outcomes.label: Excessive voltage drop or supply dips
outcomes.interpretation: Repair the feed, ground, fuse, or relay connection and recheck.

outcomes.label: Could not reach a test point
outcomes.interpretation: No change.

tests.title: Check for EGR flow at idle
tests.purpose: Determine whether exhaust gas is entering at idle through a leaking or stuck EGR valve.
procedure: At warm idle, confirm EGR is commanded closed and observe any EGR position PID.
Temporarily block EGR flow per the OEM procedure (or disconnect the valve where the OEM permits) and note changes in idle quality and misfire counts.
Restore the system and clear any codes set by the test.
tools: Block-off plate or OEM tool as specified
tests.expected: No change in idle quality or misfire counts when EGR is blocked.

outcomes.label: No change when EGR is blocked
outcomes.interpretation: EGR is not flowing at idle.

outcomes.label: Misfire stops or idle smooths with EGR blocked
outcomes.interpretation: The EGR valve is leaking or stuck open; inspect its seat for carbon.

outcomes.label: Engine has no external EGR valve
outcomes.interpretation: Not applicable; internal EGR is controlled by valve timing.

tests.title: Check cam-to-crank correlation
tests.purpose: Detect retarded valve timing from a stretched chain or worn guides.
procedure: Review the cam/crank correlation or cam position deviation PIDs at idle with the phasers parked, where available.
Alternatively, scope crank and cam signals together and compare the edge relationship with a known-good pattern for this engine.
Compare all banks and camshafts.
tools: Lab scope with at least two channels
tests.expected: Correlation within the OEM specification and matching the known-good pattern.

outcomes.label: Correlation within specification
outcomes.interpretation: Valve timing is correct.

outcomes.label: Cams retarded relative to the crank on one or all banks
outcomes.interpretation: Inspect the chain, guides, and tensioner per the OEM procedure.

outcomes.label: No known-good pattern or PID available
outcomes.interpretation: No change.

tests.title: Scope the crankshaft position signal
tests.purpose: Confirm a clean crank signal so misfire detection is trustworthy.
procedure: Back-probe the crank sensor signal and scope it at idle and while the misfire is being counted.
Look for dropouts, noise, missing or distorted teeth, and amplitude changes.
Inspect the sensor, connector, and harness routing near ignition components.
tests.expected: A clean, consistent crank signal with the expected tooth pattern.

outcomes.label: Signal clean and consistent
outcomes.interpretation: The crank signal is not the cause.

outcomes.label: Noise, dropouts, or a distorted tooth pattern
outcomes.interpretation: Repair shielding, routing, or connections, or inspect the sensor and reluctor before replacing parts.

outcomes.label: Fault not captured
outcomes.interpretation: No change; repeat during the misfire event.

tests.title: Inspect a fuel sample
tests.purpose: Check for water, debris, or the wrong fuel.
procedure: Draw a fuel sample from the service port or supply line per the OEM procedure, with fire precautions in place.
Let it settle in a clear container and look for water separation, debris, or unusual color or odor.
Where available, test alcohol content or use a water-finding paste.
tests.expected: Clear, clean fuel with no water separation or unusual odor.

outcomes.label: Fuel looks clean
outcomes.interpretation: Fuel quality is unlikely to be the cause.

outcomes.label: Water, debris, or wrong fuel found
outcomes.interpretation: Drain and flush the fuel system per the OEM procedure and replace filters as required.

outcomes.label: Could not obtain a safe sample
outcomes.interpretation: No change.

tests.title: Relative and cranking compression test (all cylinders)
tests.purpose: Check for general mechanical wear across cylinders.
procedure: Disable fuel and ignition per the OEM procedure.
Perform a relative compression test with a lab scope and high-amp probe on the starter cable.
If any cylinders appear low, confirm with a cranking compression test.
Compare cylinders with each other and with the OEM specification.
tests.expected: Compression even across cylinders and within the OEM specification.

outcomes.label: Compression even and within specification
outcomes.interpretation: General mechanical wear is unlikely.

outcomes.label: Several cylinders low or uneven
outcomes.interpretation: Follow up with leak-down testing to identify rings or valves.

outcomes.label: All cylinders evenly low
outcomes.interpretation: Suspect retarded valve timing; verify cam-to-crank correlation.

outcomes.label: Could not safely disable fuel and ignition
outcomes.interpretation: No change.

verification: Clear codes after recording the freeze frame.
Operate the vehicle at idle, cruise, and under moderate load, including a cold start.
Confirm misfire counters stay at or near zero and fuel trims are near zero (general guideline: total within roughly ±10% (general guideline — verify against OEM specification)).
Confirm Mode $06 misfire results pass and no codes return after a full drive cycle.

playbooks.title: System too lean (P0171 / P0174)
playbooks.summary: A lean code means long-term fuel trim has reached its limit adding fuel. The cause is either extra air the MAF did not measure (vacuum, gasket, PCV, duct, or purge leaks), too little fuel (low pressure or volume, restricted injectors), an under-reporting MAF, or a false lean signal (exhaust leak or skewed upstream sensor). Comparing trims at idle and at higher airflow points to the right branch: air leaks are worst at idle, while supply and MAF problems are worst under load. A two-bank lean code points to a shared cause; a one-bank code points to that bank.
clarifyingQuestions: Is one bank lean or both?
Are trims worst at idle or under load?
Any recent air filter, intake, or fuel system work, or an aftermarket or oiled air filter?
Is there a hissing noise, exhaust ticking, or hesitation under load?
Are there misfire, MAF, fuel pressure, or EVAP codes as well?

causes.title: Vacuum leak (hose, brake booster, or accessory)
causes.description: Air entering after the MAF is not measured, so the PCM adds fuel to compensate; the effect is largest at idle where total airflow is lowest.

causes.title: Intake manifold or throttle body gasket leak
causes.description: A leaking gasket admits unmetered air; on V engines it may affect one bank more than the other.

modifiers.reason: Gasket leaks are often worse cold or at idle

causes.title: PCV valve stuck open or PCV hose leak
causes.description: Excess crankcase flow or a cracked PCV hose or oil separator diaphragm adds unmetered air.

causes.title: Air leak between the MAF and the throttle body
causes.description: A cracked intake duct, loose clamp, or damaged coupler lets air bypass the MAF, often worse under load as the duct moves.

modifiers.reason: Recent air filter or intake work

causes.title: Contaminated or under-reporting MAF sensor
causes.description: Dirt or oil on the sensing element causes the MAF to under-report airflow, so the PCM under-fuels, especially at higher airflow.

causes.title: Low fuel pressure or volume (pump, filter, or regulator)
causes.description: Insufficient supply leans both banks, typically worse under load and at higher speed.

modifiers.reason: Fuel pressure or pump code present

causes.title: Restricted fuel injectors
causes.description: Deposits reduce injector flow, leaning the mixture across the affected bank or cylinders.

causes.title: Exhaust leak ahead of the upstream sensor
causes.description: Outside air drawn in through an exhaust leak makes the sensor read lean, so the PCM adds fuel although the engine is not lean.

causes.title: Upstream A/F sensor skewed (wideband systems)
causes.description: A wideband sensor that reads leaner than actual drives the PCM to add fuel and set a lean code.

causes.title: Upstream O2 sensor biased lean (narrowband systems)
causes.description: A contaminated or aged zirconia sensor biased lean drives unnecessary enrichment.

causes.title: Purge valve stuck open
causes.description: A purge valve that does not seal admits unmetered air (or vapor) at idle, shifting trims.

tests.title: Analyze fuel trims at idle, cruise, and by bank
tests.purpose: Separate air leaks (worst at idle) from fuel supply or airflow measurement problems (worst under load).
procedure: Record the freeze frame for the lean code, then warm the engine fully.
Record short-term and long-term fuel trims per bank at idle, at a steady elevated speed (for example about 2,500 rpm), and at steady cruise.
Compare the two banks on V engines.
Note whether total trim becomes more or less positive as airflow increases.
tests.expected: Total fuel trim near zero at all speeds (general guideline: within roughly ±10% (general guideline — verify against OEM specification)).

outcomes.label: Lean at idle, improving toward normal at higher airflow
outcomes.interpretation: Classic signature of a vacuum-side air leak; smoke test the intake.

outcomes.label: Lean worsens at higher airflow or under load
outcomes.interpretation: Check fuel pressure under load and MAF plausibility.

outcomes.label: Similar lean correction at all speeds
outcomes.interpretation: Suspect a sensor reporting incorrectly or an exhaust leak; verify the sensor response.

outcomes.label: Trims currently normal
outcomes.interpretation: No change; drive under the freeze frame conditions and recheck.

tests.title: Smoke test the intake, PCV, and air duct
tests.purpose: Locate unmetered air on the vacuum side or between the MAF and throttle.
procedure: Engine off. Seal the intake at the air filter housing (to include the duct) per the smoke machine instructions.
Introduce smoke and inspect the intake duct and couplers, throttle body and intake gaskets, vacuum hoses, brake booster hose, PCV valve and hoses, oil fill cap, and dipstick seal.
Remove the equipment and reconnect everything.
tests.expected: No smoke escapes anywhere in the intake or PCV system.

outcomes.label: No smoke escapes
outcomes.interpretation: No intake leak; move on to fuel supply, MAF, and sensor checks.

outcomes.label: Smoke at a vacuum hose, brake booster hose, or accessory
outcomes.interpretation: Repair the leak and recheck trims.

outcomes.label: Smoke at the intake manifold or throttle body gasket
outcomes.interpretation: Replace the gasket per the OEM procedure and recheck trims.

outcomes.label: Smoke at the PCV valve, hoses, separator, oil cap, or dipstick
outcomes.interpretation: Repair the PCV leak and recheck trims.

outcomes.label: Smoke at the duct, coupler, or clamp between the MAF and throttle
outcomes.interpretation: Replace the duct or coupler and recheck trims.

outcomes.label: Could not seal the intake
outcomes.interpretation: No change; try propane enrichment with fire precautions.

tests.title: Check the purge valve for leakage at idle
tests.purpose: Determine whether a purge valve that does not seal is leaning the idle.
procedure: At warm idle with purge commanded off, note fuel trims.
Pinch or cap the purge line at the intake side (per the OEM procedure) and watch whether trims drop.
Alternatively, apply vacuum to the purge valve with it unpowered and check that it holds.
Restore connections and clear any EVAP codes set by the test.
tests.expected: Trims do not change when the purge line is blocked, and the valve holds vacuum when unpowered.

outcomes.label: Purge valve seals
outcomes.interpretation: The purge valve is not the cause.

outcomes.label: Trims drop when the line is blocked, or the valve will not hold vacuum
outcomes.interpretation: Replace the purge valve and check the canister for fuel or charcoal contamination.

outcomes.label: Could not access the purge line
outcomes.interpretation: No change.

tests.title: Check fuel pressure and volume under load
tests.purpose: Confirm fuel supply meets demand at higher airflow.
procedure: Connect a fuel pressure gauge (port injection) or monitor the low-side and rail pressure PIDs (direct injection) per the OEM procedure.
Record pressure at idle, during a snap, and during a loaded road test with a helper.
Compare actual with desired and with the OEM specification; perform a volume test if pressure is marginal.
Check for leaks at the gauge connection before and after the test.
tests.expected: Pressure and volume within the OEM specification and pressure steady under load.

outcomes.label: Pressure and volume adequate
outcomes.interpretation: Fuel supply is not the cause.

outcomes.label: Pressure or volume low, or pressure sags under load
outcomes.interpretation: Diagnose the pump, filter, regulator, and pump circuit before replacing parts.

outcomes.label: Could not connect a gauge
outcomes.interpretation: No change.

tests.title: Check MAF plausibility and inspect the element
tests.purpose: Determine whether the MAF is under-reporting airflow.
procedure: At warm idle, compare MAF airflow with the expected value (general guideline: roughly equal in grams per second to engine displacement in liters (general guideline — verify against OEM specification)).
During a safe wide-open-throttle acceleration, record peak MAF and compare it with expected airflow for the engine.
Watch whether fuel trims move toward zero when the MAF is unplugged briefly at idle (the PCM falls back to calculated airflow).
Key off: inspect the element for oil, dust, or damage and inspect the filter and duct.
tests.expected: MAF readings plausible for the engine and the element clean (values per OEM specification).

outcomes.label: MAF readings plausible and element clean
outcomes.interpretation: The MAF is not the cause.

outcomes.label: MAF reads low, trims improve with MAF unplugged, or element contaminated
outcomes.interpretation: Clean with MAF-safe cleaner if the OEM allows, fix the contamination source, and retest before replacing.

outcomes.label: Could not perform the loaded test safely
outcomes.interpretation: No change.

tests.title: Upstream O2 / A/F sensor response test (induced rich and lean)
tests.purpose: Determine whether the upstream oxygen or air/fuel ratio sensor reports mixture changes accurately and quickly, separating a sensor fault from a true lean or rich condition.
procedure: Identify the upstream sensor type (narrowband zirconia O2 or wideband A/F) from service information; this changes how the data is read.
Warm the engine to full operating temperature and confirm closed-loop operation. Check for exhaust leaks ahead of the sensor first; a leak invalidates this test.
Graph the upstream sensor signal (voltage, current, or lambda/equivalence ratio PID) for each bank at idle and at a steady elevated engine speed.
Induce a rich condition (a brief snap of the throttle, or a controlled amount of propane at the intake) and observe how quickly the sensor reports rich.
Induce a lean condition (a brief deceleration with fuel cut, or a controlled vacuum leak) and observe how quickly the sensor reports lean.
Compare the responses between banks and with the fuel trims; the sensor should track every mixture change promptly.
tests.expected: The sensor follows each induced rich and lean change quickly and fully, and both banks behave alike (response time per OEM specification; a narrowband sensor generally swings well above and below its midpoint (general guideline — verify against OEM specification)).

outcomes.label: Sensor responds quickly and fully to induced rich and lean changes
outcomes.interpretation: The sensor is reporting accurately; any lean or rich reading reflects the actual mixture, so look for the underlying cause.

outcomes.label: Response is slow, reduced in amplitude, or noticeably worse than the other bank
outcomes.interpretation: The sensor is aged or contaminated. Check the heater and look for contamination sources before replacing it.

outcomes.label: Sensor stays biased lean or rich, or does not respond to an induced change
outcomes.interpretation: The signal is not believable. Test the signal and heater circuits before condemning the sensor.

outcomes.label: Exhaust leak present or closed loop could not be achieved
outcomes.interpretation: No change; repair any exhaust leak ahead of the sensor or resolve the open-loop cause, then repeat.

tests.title: Inspect for exhaust leaks ahead of the upstream sensor
tests.purpose: Rule out a false lean signal caused by outside air entering the exhaust.
procedure: With the engine cold, start it and listen for ticking or puffing at the manifold, flange, and flex pipe ahead of the sensor.
Engine off and cool: inspect for black soot trails, cracked manifolds, broken studs, and loose flanges.
Optionally introduce smoke into the tailpipe at low pressure with the engine off and look for leaks ahead of the sensor.
tests.expected: No leaks or soot trails ahead of the upstream sensor.

outcomes.label: No exhaust leak found
outcomes.interpretation: The sensor is seeing true exhaust gas.

outcomes.label: Leak, soot trail, or broken stud found ahead of the sensor
outcomes.interpretation: Repair the leak and recheck trims before any sensor replacement.

outcomes.label: Could not inspect the full area
outcomes.interpretation: No change.

tests.title: Injector balance or flow comparison
tests.purpose: Identify restricted injectors that lean the mixture.
procedure: Port injection: perform an injector balance (pressure drop) test per the OEM procedure with fire precautions in place, or compare off-vehicle flow on a cleaning bench.
Direct injection: use OEM injector balance or cylinder contribution tests; do not open the high-pressure system.
Compare each injector with the others and with the OEM allowable variation.
tools: Fuel pressure gauge and injector pulser
tests.expected: All injectors flow within the OEM allowable variation.

outcomes.label: Injectors balanced
outcomes.interpretation: Injector restriction is unlikely.

outcomes.label: One or more injectors low
outcomes.interpretation: Clean or replace the affected injectors per the OEM procedure and recheck trims.

outcomes.label: Could not perform a balance test on this system
outcomes.interpretation: No change.

verification: Clear codes after recording the freeze frame.
Confirm short-term and long-term fuel trims are near zero at idle and cruise (general guideline: total within roughly ±10% (general guideline — verify against OEM specification)).
Complete a drive cycle and confirm the lean code does not return and the fuel system monitor passes.

playbooks.title: System too rich (P0172 / P0175)
playbooks.summary: A rich code means long-term fuel trim has reached its limit removing fuel. Extra fuel can come from high fuel pressure, a leaking regulator diaphragm or injector, canister vapor through a stuck-open purge valve, or fuel-diluted oil drawn in through the PCV system. The PCM may also be misled by a MAF or MAP reading high, an ECT reading cold, a thermostat that keeps the engine cold, or a skewed upstream sensor. Characterize when the engine runs rich first, then isolate purge and PCV sources before testing fuel pressure and sensors.
clarifyingQuestions: Is one bank rich or both?
Is it worse at idle, after refueling, after a hot soak, or during warm-up?
Does the temperature gauge reach normal, and does the heater get hot?
Does the oil smell of fuel or is the oil level above full?
Any recent fuel, sensor, or EVAP work, or a habit of topping off the tank?

causes.title: Fuel pressure regulator stuck closed or leaking diaphragm
causes.description: Excessive fuel pressure, or fuel drawn through a ruptured diaphragm into the intake, delivers more fuel than commanded (return-style port injection systems).

causes.title: Leaking or dripping fuel injector
causes.description: A leaking injector adds uncommanded fuel, often causing a rich start after a hot soak and a rich idle.

causes.title: Purge valve stuck open with a loaded canister
causes.description: Fuel vapor from the canister enters the intake continuously, richening the mixture at idle and especially after refueling.

causes.title: MAF sensor over-reporting airflow
causes.description: A MAF reading higher than actual makes the PCM inject too much fuel.

causes.title: MAP sensor reading higher than actual (speed-density fueling)
causes.description: On engines that calculate airflow from MAP, a sensor or hose fault that reads high over-fuels the engine.

causes.title: Coolant temperature sensor reading colder than actual
causes.description: The PCM adds cold-engine enrichment when the ECT signal indicates a colder engine than actual.

causes.title: Thermostat stuck open or opening early
causes.description: An engine that never reaches operating temperature keeps some warm-up enrichment active.

modifiers.reason: Low heat or low gauge reading

causes.title: Upstream A/F sensor skewed rich (wideband systems)
causes.description: A wideband sensor that reads richer than actual makes the PCM remove fuel and can set a rich code without a true rich condition.

causes.title: Upstream O2 sensor biased rich (narrowband systems)
causes.description: A contaminated sensor (silicone, coolant, or fuel additives) can read rich and mislead fuel control.

causes.title: Fuel-diluted engine oil feeding vapor through the PCV system
causes.description: Fuel in the crankcase evaporates and is drawn in through the PCV system, adding unmetered fuel; common with short trips, leaking injectors, or direct-injection wash-down.

modifiers.reason: Short trips or oil smells of fuel

causes.title: Restricted air filter or intake (speed-density engines)
causes.description: A severely restricted intake reduces airflow; on engines that do not meter air with a MAF this can leave the mixture rich.

modifiers.reason: Air filter or intake debris concern

tests.title: Analyze fuel trims at idle, cruise, cold, and after refueling
tests.purpose: Characterize when the rich condition occurs to separate vapor, leak, sensor, and temperature causes.
procedure: Record the freeze frame for the rich code, including ECT and load.
Record short-term and long-term fuel trims per bank at idle and cruise, cold and fully warm.
Note whether trims become more negative at idle after a hot soak or after refueling.
Compare the two banks on V engines.
tests.expected: Total fuel trim near zero in all conditions (general guideline: within roughly ±10% (general guideline — verify against OEM specification)).

outcomes.label: Most negative at idle, after a hot soak or after refueling
outcomes.interpretation: Check the purge valve, PCV fuel vapor, and injector leakage.

outcomes.label: Rich correction at all speeds and loads
outcomes.interpretation: Check fuel pressure, airflow sensor plausibility, and the upstream sensor response.

outcomes.label: Rich mainly during warm-up, or ECT stays below normal
outcomes.interpretation: Verify ECT plausibility and thermostat operation.

outcomes.label: Trims currently normal
outcomes.interpretation: No change; recheck under the freeze frame conditions.

tests.title: Check fuel pressure, regulator, and leak-down
tests.purpose: Detect excessive fuel pressure, a leaking regulator diaphragm, or leaking injectors.
procedure: Port injection: connect a fuel pressure gauge per the OEM procedure with fire precautions in place.
Compare running pressure with the OEM specification; on vacuum-referenced regulators, check that pressure changes with vacuum and that no fuel is present in the regulator vacuum hose.
Shut the engine off and watch pressure decay over the time given in service information.
If pressure drops, isolate the pump check valve and regulator by clamping the lines where the OEM permits to find whether injectors are leaking.
Direct injection: compare rail pressure actual and desired PIDs; do not open the high-pressure system.
tools: Line clamps approved for fuel hose
tests.expected: Pressure within specification, regulator responds correctly, no fuel in the vacuum hose, and pressure holds after shutdown per the OEM specification.

outcomes.label: Pressure, regulation, and hold all normal
outcomes.interpretation: The fuel pressure system is not over-fueling.

outcomes.label: Pressure too high, does not respond to vacuum, or fuel in the regulator hose
outcomes.interpretation: Replace the regulator (or repair a restricted return line) and recheck trims.

outcomes.label: Pressure bleeds down with the pump and regulator isolated
outcomes.interpretation: An injector is leaking; identify it (plug inspection, borescope, or pressure isolation) before replacement.

outcomes.label: No test port or direct-injection only
outcomes.interpretation: No change; rely on PIDs and other tests.

tests.title: Isolate the purge system and watch fuel trims
tests.purpose: Determine whether canister vapor through a leaking purge valve is richening the mixture.
procedure: At warm idle, confirm purge is commanded off and note trims.
Pinch or cap the purge line at the intake side per the OEM procedure.
Watch whether short-term trim rises toward zero within a short time.
Check the purge valve's ability to hold vacuum unpowered, and check the canister and lines for liquid fuel.
Restore connections and clear any EVAP codes set by the test.
tests.expected: No change in trims when purge is blocked; valve holds vacuum unpowered.

outcomes.label: Trims unchanged; valve seals
outcomes.interpretation: Purge vapor is not the cause.

outcomes.label: Trims move toward zero with purge blocked, or the valve leaks
outcomes.interpretation: Replace the purge valve and inspect the canister for liquid fuel (often from overfilling).

outcomes.label: Could not access the purge line
outcomes.interpretation: No change.

tests.title: Check engine oil for fuel dilution
tests.purpose: Determine whether fuel vapor from the crankcase is richening the mixture.
procedure: Check the oil level and smell the dipstick for fuel; note an oil level above the full mark.
At warm idle, temporarily disconnect or block the PCV feed to the intake per the OEM procedure (cap the intake port) and watch trims.
Restore the PCV system immediately after the check.
If dilution is confirmed, look for the source (leaking injectors, short-trip use) before changing the oil.
tests.expected: No fuel odor, normal oil level, and trims unchanged when PCV flow is blocked.

outcomes.label: No sign of fuel in the oil
outcomes.interpretation: Crankcase fuel vapor is not the cause.

outcomes.label: Oil smells of fuel or level is high, and trims improve with PCV blocked
outcomes.interpretation: Change the oil after finding the source of the fuel, then recheck trims.

outcomes.label: Results unclear
outcomes.interpretation: No change; consider an oil analysis.

tests.title: Check MAF and MAP plausibility
tests.purpose: Detect an airflow or pressure sensor that over-reports and drives over-fueling.
procedure: Key on, engine off: MAF should read near zero and MAP should match BARO.

At warm idle, compare MAF with the expected value (general guideline: roughly equal in grams per second to engine displacement in liters (general guideline — verify against OEM specification)) and MAP with a vacuum gauge.
Unplug the MAF briefly at idle (where the PCM falls back to calculated airflow) and watch whether trims move toward zero.
Inspect the MAP sensor hose and port for fuel, oil, or blockage.
tests.expected: MAF and MAP readings plausible and consistent with each other (values per OEM specification).

outcomes.label: MAF and MAP readings plausible
outcomes.interpretation: Airflow sensing is not over-reporting.

outcomes.label: MAF reads high or trims improve with the MAF unplugged
outcomes.interpretation: Check the MAF circuit and connector, then replace the sensor if the circuit is good.

outcomes.label: MAP reads higher than the gauge or BARO
outcomes.interpretation: Check the MAP hose and circuit, then replace the sensor if needed.

outcomes.label: Engine lacks the sensor or data is unavailable
outcomes.interpretation: No change.

tests.title: ECT plausibility: cold-soak comparison and warm-up curve
tests.purpose: Confirm that the coolant temperature sensor reads the actual engine temperature and that the engine warms up normally.
procedure: After a cold soak (engine off for several hours), compare ECT, IAT, and ambient temperature PIDs; they should be close to each other.
Start the engine and graph ECT during warm-up at idle and then at a steady speed, noting the time to reach normal operating temperature.
Measure the actual temperature at the thermostat housing or near the ECT sensor with an infrared or contact thermometer and compare it with the PID.
Feel or measure the upper radiator hose; it should stay cool until the thermostat opens, then warm quickly.
tests.expected: ECT agrees with the other temperature PIDs after a cold soak, tracks the measured temperature, and reaches normal operating temperature within the expected time (warm-up time and thermostat opening temperature per OEM specification).

outcomes.label: ECT is plausible and warm-up is normal
outcomes.interpretation: Coolant temperature sensing and thermostat control are normal.

outcomes.label: ECT PID disagrees with the cold-soak temperatures or with the measured temperature
outcomes.interpretation: The ECT sensor or its circuit is skewed; check the circuit and connector before replacing the sensor.

outcomes.label: ECT is accurate, but the engine warms slowly or never reaches operating temperature; upper hose warms early
outcomes.interpretation: The thermostat is opening early or stuck open.

outcomes.label: Could not cold soak or observe a full warm-up
outcomes.interpretation: No change; repeat after the vehicle sits overnight.

tests.title: Inspect the air filter and intake for restriction
tests.purpose: Rule out a restricted intake on speed-density engines.
procedure: Engine off: remove and inspect the air filter for heavy dirt, water, or debris.
Inspect the inlet duct and snorkel for debris, nests, or a collapsed section.
Optionally measure intake restriction with a gauge at wide-open throttle and compare with the OEM specification.
tests.expected: Clean filter and unobstructed intake path.

outcomes.label: Filter and duct clear
outcomes.interpretation: Intake restriction is not the cause.

Refuel and recheck trims if the complaint was related to refueling.

playbooks.title: Oxygen / A/F sensor circuit and response
playbooks.summary: Oxygen and air/fuel ratio sensor codes cover circuit faults, slow response, range and performance faults, and stuck-lean or stuck-rich signals. First decide whether the code is a circuit problem (signal at a default or rail value) or a performance problem (active but slow or biased). A true lean or rich mixture, an exhaust leak ahead of the sensor, or a heater that does not bring the sensor to temperature can all make a good sensor look bad. Prove the sensor response, heater, and wiring, and look for contamination sources before replacing a sensor.
clarifyingQuestions: Which bank and sensor position is set, and is it an upstream or downstream sensor?
Does the vehicle use a wideband A/F sensor or a narrowband O2 sensor upstream?
Has the sensor or any exhaust component been replaced recently?
Is there coolant loss, oil consumption, or an exhaust tick?
Are there heater, lean, rich, or misfire codes as well?

causes.title: Aged or failed O2 sensor
causes.description: An aged zirconia sensor responds slowly, with reduced amplitude, or not at all, setting slow-response, range/performance, or stuck codes.

modifiers.reason: Response or downstream sensor code present
Stuck lean or rich code present

causes.title: Failed or aged wideband A/F sensor
causes.description: A worn wideband sensor reports an incorrect or slow lambda value; circuit and pump-current codes are common with internal faults.

modifiers.reason: A/F sensor circuit or performance code present
Vehicle uses a wideband A/F sensor

causes.title: Sensor poisoned by silicone, coolant, oil, or fuel additives
causes.description: Contaminants coat the sensing element and slow its response; replacing the sensor without fixing the source leads to repeat failure.

causes.title: Exhaust leak ahead of the sensor
causes.description: Outside air pulled in at a leak dilutes the exhaust at the sensor, causing false lean readings and erratic response.

causes.title: Sensor heater not bringing the sensor to temperature
causes.description: A sensor that is not heated properly switches slowly or not at all, especially at idle and after a cold start.

causes.title: Damaged sensor signal or reference wiring
causes.description: Wiring melted on the exhaust, chafed, or shorted to the heater circuit distorts the signal and sets circuit codes.

modifiers.reason: Recent exhaust work or wiring damage noted

causes.title: Corroded or water-intruded sensor connector
causes.description: Corrosion adds resistance or leakage to the low-level signal, causing erratic readings or circuit codes.

causes.title: True lean condition from an intake leak
causes.description: A real lean mixture can make a healthy sensor appear stuck lean or out of range.

causes.title: Incorrect sensor installed or connectors swapped
causes.description: A sensor with the wrong characteristics, or bank connectors crossed after service, causes implausible readings.

modifiers.reason: O2 sensor signals swapped code present

causes.title: PCM calibration requiring an update
causes.description: Some sensor monitors have been revised by calibration updates to address false failures.

tests.title: Review codes, sensor data, and fuel trims
tests.purpose: Identify which sensor is affected and whether the code is a circuit fault, a performance fault, or a true mixture problem.
procedure: Record every code and freeze frame, including heater and fuel trim codes.
Identify the sensor location (bank and sensor number) and type from service information.
Graph the affected sensor and fuel trims at warm idle and at a steady elevated speed.
Note whether the signal is fixed at a default value, erratic, slow, or biased.
tests.expected: Sensor signal active and plausible, with fuel trims near zero (general guideline: total within roughly ±10% (general guideline — verify against OEM specification)).

outcomes.label: Signal fixed at a default or rail value, with circuit codes
outcomes.interpretation: Test the signal, reference, and heater circuits before the sensor.

outcomes.label: Signal active but slow, reduced, or biased, with trims near normal
outcomes.interpretation: Perform a response test and check heater operation.

outcomes.label: Sensor reads lean and trims are strongly positive
outcomes.interpretation: The mixture may really be lean, or an exhaust leak is fooling the sensor; check for leaks first.

outcomes.label: Signal currently looks normal
outcomes.interpretation: No change; recheck under the freeze frame conditions.

tests.title: Inspect for exhaust leaks ahead of the sensor
tests.purpose: Rule out outside air entering the exhaust ahead of the sensor.
procedure: With the engine cold, start it and listen for ticking or puffing at the manifold, flanges, and flex pipe ahead of the sensor.
Engine off and cool: inspect for soot trails, cracks, broken studs, and loose flanges, including around the sensor boss.
Optionally introduce low-pressure smoke into the tailpipe with the engine off.
tests.expected: No leaks ahead of the sensor.

outcomes.label: No exhaust leak found
outcomes.interpretation: The sensor is seeing true exhaust gas.

outcomes.label: Leak found ahead of the sensor
outcomes.interpretation: Repair the leak and recheck sensor operation before replacing the sensor.

outcomes.label: Could not inspect the full area
outcomes.interpretation: No change.

tests.title: Check sensor heater operation
tests.purpose: Confirm the heater brings the sensor to operating temperature.
procedure: Check for heater codes and heater status or current PIDs where available.
Key off: disconnect the sensor and measure heater element resistance, comparing with the OEM specification at the stated temperature.
Check heater supply voltage with key on and the ground or control side with the heater commanded on.
Reconnect and confirm the signal becomes active quickly after a cold start.
tests.expected: Heater resistance, supply, and control within the OEM specification, and the sensor becomes active promptly after start-up.

outcomes.label: Heater operates normally
outcomes.interpretation: The heater is not the cause.

outcomes.label: Heater open, out of specification, or not powered or controlled
outcomes.interpretation: Follow the heater circuit diagnosis: element, supply fuse, wiring, then PCM control.

outcomes.label: Heater circuit not accessible
outcomes.interpretation: No change.

tests.title: Test the sensor signal and reference circuits
tests.purpose: Find open, shorted, or high-resistance wiring and connector faults.
procedure: Key off: inspect the harness along the exhaust for melting, chafing, and correct routing; inspect the connector for corrosion, water, and spread terminals.
Key on, sensor unplugged: measure the PCM bias or reference voltage on the signal circuits and compare with the OEM specification.
Check each signal circuit for continuity, shorts to ground, shorts to voltage, and shorts to the heater circuit.
Wiggle the harness while monitoring the signal with the sensor connected.
tests.expected: Reference or bias voltage correct, no opens or shorts, and a stable signal during the wiggle test.

outcomes.label: Circuits and connector good
outcomes.interpretation: Wiring is not the cause; focus on the sensor itself.

outcomes.label: Open, short, or chafed or melted wiring found
outcomes.interpretation: Repair the wiring per OEM repair guidelines and reroute away from heat.

outcomes.label: Corroded, wet, or loose connector terminals
outcomes.interpretation: Repair or replace the connector terminals; do not use sealants or contact grease unless approved by the OEM.

outcomes.label: Could not access the circuits
outcomes.interpretation: No change.

tests.title: Remove and inspect the sensor tip
tests.purpose: Look for contamination that explains a slow or biased sensor and points to a root cause.
procedure: Remove the sensor with the correct socket once the exhaust is safe to work on (penetrating oil on a warm exhaust may be needed; avoid burns).
Inspect the protective shield and element for white or gritty deposits (silicone), green or white crust (coolant), black oily deposits (oil), or reddish deposits (fuel additives).
Compare with the other bank's sensor if accessible.
Reinstall or replace using anti-seize only if the OEM specifies it, and avoid getting it on the tip.
tests.expected: Light gray or tan deposits with no signs of contamination.

outcomes.label: Normal deposits only
outcomes.interpretation: No contamination; a slow sensor is due to age.

outcomes.label: Silicone, coolant, oil, or additive deposits found
outcomes.interpretation: Find and fix the source (coolant leak, oil consumption, sealant, or additive) before installing a new sensor.

outcomes.label: Sensor seized; not removed
outcomes.interpretation: No change; defer until the sensor must be replaced.

tests.title: Verify sensor part number and connector positions
tests.purpose: Rule out an incorrect sensor or crossed connectors after recent service.
procedure: Compare the installed sensor part number with the OEM catalog for this vehicle and position.
Trace each sensor harness to its connector and confirm bank 1 and bank 2 are not swapped.
Confirm the sensor is the correct type (narrowband or wideband) for the position.
tests.expected: Correct sensors installed and connected to the correct harness positions.

outcomes.label: Correct parts and connections
outcomes.interpretation: Installation is correct.

outcomes.label: Wrong sensor or swapped connectors found
outcomes.interpretation: Install the correct sensor or correct the connections, then clear codes and retest.

outcomes.label: Could not verify the part
outcomes.interpretation: No change.

tests.title: Check downstream sensor activity under forced lean and rich
tests.purpose: Confirm a downstream sensor can still read both lean and rich for codes on sensor 2 or sensor 3.
procedure: Warm the engine fully and confirm closed loop.
At steady cruise or elevated idle, note the downstream signal; it is normally steadier than the upstream signal.
Force lean with a deceleration fuel cut and confirm the signal drops to a lean reading.
Force rich with a brief wide-open-throttle event (or propane) and confirm it rises to a rich reading.
Compare both banks.
tests.expected: The downstream sensor reaches clear lean and rich readings when forced (values per OEM specification).

outcomes.label: Downstream sensor reads lean and rich when forced
outcomes.interpretation: The downstream sensor responds; review circuit or catalyst issues instead.

outcomes.label: Downstream sensor stuck or will not reach lean or rich
outcomes.interpretation: Check wiring and connector, then replace the sensor if the circuit is good.

outcomes.label: Only upstream codes present; not applicable
outcomes.interpretation: No change.

tests.title: Check for a true lean condition
tests.purpose: Determine whether the engine is actually lean rather than the sensor misreporting.
procedure: Smoke test the intake and PCV system with the engine off.
Optionally measure tailpipe gases with a five-gas analyzer at warm idle and at a steady elevated speed and compare with the sensor readings.
Restore all connections.
tests.expected: No intake leaks, and gas readings agree with the sensor.

outcomes.label: No leak; mixture not actually lean
outcomes.interpretation: The sensor or its circuit is misreporting.

outcomes.label: Intake leak found or the engine is actually lean
outcomes.interpretation: Repair the leak and recheck; the sensor may be fine.

outcomes.label: Results unclear
outcomes.interpretation: No change.

tests.title: Check technical service bulletins and PCM software level
tests.purpose: Identify known pattern failures, revised parts, or calibration updates for oxygen or A/F sensor monitors.
procedure: Search OEM service information for bulletins, campaigns, and recalls that match the codes and symptoms for this vehicle.
Read the current PCM calibration ID with a scan tool and compare it with the latest available calibration.
Note any bulletin-directed diagnostic steps or revised parts before continuing.
tools: Scan tool with calibration ID readout
tests.expected: No applicable bulletin and the PCM calibration is current.

outcomes.label: No applicable bulletin; calibration current
outcomes.interpretation: Software and known pattern failures are unlikely; continue with testing.

outcomes.label: Applicable bulletin or calibration update found
outcomes.interpretation: Follow the bulletin procedure, then verify the repair before replacing other parts.

outcomes.label: Service information not available
outcomes.interpretation: No change; continue with direct testing.

verification: Clear codes after recording the freeze frame.
Confirm the sensor switches or reports lambda changes promptly and both banks behave alike.
Confirm fuel trims are near zero (general guideline: total within roughly ±10% (general guideline — verify against OEM specification)).
Complete a drive cycle and confirm the oxygen sensor monitor passes with no codes returning.

playbooks.title: Oxygen / A/F sensor heater circuit
playbooks.summary: Heater codes mean the PCM detected an open, short, or poor performance in the heater that brings an O2 or A/F sensor to operating temperature. Start by noting whether one heater or several are affected: several at once points to a shared fuse, feed, or low system voltage, while one points to that sensor, its connector, or its wiring. Test supply, element resistance, and the control circuit in order, and suspect the PCM driver only after the wiring and element are proven good.
clarifyingQuestions: Which bank and sensor positions have heater codes?
Are any fuses blown or other heaters affected?
Has the sensor or exhaust been replaced recently?
Is the code current or intermittent, and does it set only on cold starts?
Is there any charging or battery concern?

causes.title: Failed heater element inside the sensor
causes.description: The heater element in the sensor opens or shorts with age and thermal cycling; the sensor then warms slowly and the PCM sets a heater code.

modifiers.reason: Heater resistance or performance code present

causes.title: Heater supply fuse, relay, or feed circuit fault
causes.description: Heaters are usually fed from a shared fused supply; a blown fuse or open feed disables several heaters at once.

modifiers.reason: Multiple heaters or a fuse suspected

causes.title: Heater control or supply wiring damaged
causes.description: Heater wires routed near the exhaust can melt or chafe, causing open or shorted heater circuits.

modifiers.reason: Recent exhaust work or wiring damage

causes.title: Corroded, wet, or heat-damaged heater connector
causes.description: Heater current is relatively high, so a poor connection overheats and causes intermittent heater codes.

causes.title: PCM heater driver fault
causes.description: A failed low-side driver in the PCM cannot switch the heater on; confirm only after the heater and wiring test good.

causes.title: Incorrect sensor with mismatched heater
causes.description: A sensor with a different heater characteristic from the OEM part can set heater performance codes.

causes.title: Low or unstable system voltage
causes.description: Low charging voltage reduces heater current and can set heater performance codes.

modifiers.reason: System voltage or charging code present

causes.title: PCM calibration requiring an update
causes.description: Some heater monitors have been revised by calibration updates.

tests.title: Review heater codes across all sensors
tests.purpose: Decide whether one heater or several heaters are affected, which points to the sensor or to a shared feed.
procedure: Record all heater codes and freeze frames, including system voltage.
Note which bank and sensor positions are affected and whether the codes are circuit (open, low, high) or performance/resistance codes.
Review heater status or current PIDs where available.
tests.expected: Only one heater affected, with system voltage normal.

outcomes.label: Only one sensor's heater is affected
outcomes.interpretation: Focus on that sensor, its connector, and its circuit.

outcomes.label: Several heaters affected at once
outcomes.interpretation: Check the shared fuse and feed, and system voltage.

outcomes.label: Codes are history only and not currently set
outcomes.interpretation: No change; recheck after a cold start.

tests.title: Check heater supply voltage and fuse
tests.purpose: Confirm the heater receives battery voltage with the key on or engine running.
procedure: Inspect the heater fuse (and relay if used) identified in the wiring diagram.
Back-probe the heater supply terminal at the sensor connector and measure voltage with the key on (and engine running if the design requires).
If voltage is missing or low, perform voltage drop testing along the feed.
tests.expected: Supply voltage at the connector close to battery voltage (allowable drop per OEM specification).

outcomes.label: Supply present and within the allowable drop
outcomes.interpretation: The feed is not the cause; check the element and control circuit.

outcomes.label: No or low supply voltage, or fuse blown
outcomes.interpretation: Repair the feed; if the fuse was blown, find the short (often a heater element or chafed wire) before replacing it.

outcomes.label: Could not access the connector
outcomes.interpretation: No change.

tests.title: Measure heater element resistance
tests.purpose: Check the heater element inside the sensor.
procedure: Key off: disconnect the sensor connector.
Measure resistance across the heater terminals on the sensor side and compare with the OEM specification at the stated temperature.
Check for continuity between the heater and signal terminals and between the heater and the sensor body (should be open).
tests.expected: Heater resistance within the OEM specification and no short to the signal circuit or sensor body.

outcomes.label: Heater resistance within specification
outcomes.interpretation: The heater element is good; check the wiring and control.

outcomes.label: Heater open, shorted, or out of specification
outcomes.interpretation: Replace the sensor with the correct OEM-specified part.

outcomes.label: Could not measure at the specified temperature
outcomes.interpretation: No change; repeat when conditions match.

tests.title: Test the heater control circuit and PCM driver
tests.purpose: Check the control (ground) side wiring and whether the PCM switches the heater.
procedure: Key off: check the control wire between the sensor connector and the PCM for continuity and shorts to ground or voltage.
Reconnect and, with the heater commanded on, scope or measure the control side for switching (duty cycle or low voltage when on).
If the wiring is good and no control is present, check PCM powers and grounds before considering a driver fault.
tests.expected: Control wire intact and the PCM switches the heater as commanded.

outcomes.label: Wiring intact and heater switched normally
outcomes.interpretation: The control circuit and PCM driver are working.

outcomes.label: Open, short, or high resistance in the control wire
outcomes.interpretation: Repair the wiring and reroute it away from the exhaust.

outcomes.label: Wiring good but no switching from the PCM
outcomes.interpretation: Verify PCM power and ground and check for software updates before replacing or reprogramming the PCM.

outcomes.label: Could not access the control circuit
outcomes.interpretation: No change.

tests.title: Inspect the heater connector and harness routing
tests.purpose: Find corroded, loose, or heat-damaged terminals and melted wiring.
procedure: Key off: disconnect the sensor connector and inspect both halves for corrosion, water, discoloration, melted plastic, and spread terminals.
Check terminal tension with the correct test probe.
Inspect the harness along the exhaust for melting, missing clips, and chafing.
tests.expected: Clean, tight terminals and wiring clipped away from heat.

outcomes.label: Connector and routing good
outcomes.interpretation: Connector is not the cause.

outcomes.label: Corroded, loose, or heat-damaged terminals
outcomes.interpretation: Repair or replace the terminals and connector per OEM guidelines.

outcomes.label: Harness melted, chafed, or unclipped near the exhaust
outcomes.interpretation: Repair the wiring and restore correct routing and clips.

outcomes.label: Connector not accessible
outcomes.interpretation: No change.

tests.title: Check charging voltage while running
tests.purpose: Rule out low system voltage as the reason for heater performance codes.
procedure: Measure battery voltage at the battery with the engine running at idle and at an elevated speed with electrical loads on.
Compare with the PCM system voltage PID.
If low, follow charging system diagnosis.
tests.expected: Charging voltage within the OEM specification and PCM voltage PID in agreement.

outcomes.label: Charging voltage normal
outcomes.interpretation: System voltage is not the cause.

outcomes.label: Charging voltage low or PCM sees low voltage
outcomes.interpretation: Diagnose the charging system and PCM feed before the heater.

outcomes.label: Could not measure
outcomes.interpretation: No change.

tests.title: Verify the installed sensor is the correct part
tests.purpose: Rule out a sensor whose heater does not match the OEM design.
procedure: Compare the installed sensor part number with the OEM catalog for this position.
Check whether the code began after a sensor replacement.
Confirm the connector matches without modification or splicing.
tests.expected: Correct OEM-specified sensor installed without harness modification.

outcomes.label: Correct part installed
outcomes.interpretation: Part selection is not the cause.

outcomes.label: Non-matching sensor or spliced connector found
outcomes.interpretation: Install the correct sensor and repair any splices.

outcomes.label: Could not verify the part
outcomes.interpretation: No change.

tests.title: Check technical service bulletins and PCM software level
tests.purpose: Identify known pattern failures, revised parts, or calibration updates for oxygen sensor heater monitors.
procedure: Search OEM service information for bulletins, campaigns, and recalls that match the codes and symptoms for this vehicle.
Read the current PCM calibration ID with a scan tool and compare it with the latest available calibration.
Note any bulletin-directed diagnostic steps or revised parts before continuing.
tools: Scan tool with calibration ID readout
tests.expected: No applicable bulletin and the PCM calibration is current.
