outcomes.label: No applicable bulletin; calibration current
outcomes.interpretation: Software and known pattern failures are unlikely; continue with testing.

outcomes.label: Applicable bulletin or calibration update found
outcomes.interpretation: Follow the bulletin procedure, then verify the repair before replacing other parts.

outcomes.label: Service information not available
outcomes.interpretation: No change; continue with direct testing.

verification: Clear codes after recording the freeze frame.
Perform a cold start and confirm the heater status PIDs (where available) show the heater operating and the sensor becomes active promptly.
Complete the heater monitor drive cycle and confirm no heater codes return.

playbooks.title: Catalyst efficiency below threshold (P0420 / P0430)
playbooks.summary: The catalyst monitor compares upstream and downstream sensor activity to estimate how much oxygen the converter stores. Before condemning the converter, confirm the engine has no misfire or fuel control faults, the upstream sensor responds correctly, the downstream sensor and wiring are sound, and there are no exhaust leaks ahead of the downstream sensor. Check for oil or coolant consumption that would ruin a replacement, verify the converter is the correct certified part, and check for software updates.
clarifyingQuestions: Which bank is affected, and are there any other codes (misfire, fuel trim, sensors)?
Has the converter, an O2 sensor, or any exhaust component been replaced?
Is there oil or coolant consumption, or blue or white smoke?
Is there an exhaust leak noise or rattle from the converter?
What is the vehicle mileage and driving pattern?

causes.title: Catalytic converter with reduced oxygen storage
causes.description: An aged, overheated, or contaminated converter no longer stores oxygen, so the downstream sensor starts to mirror the upstream sensor.

modifiers.reason: History of misfire or fuel trim faults that can damage the converter

causes.title: Lazy or biased O2 sensor (usually downstream)
causes.description: A downstream sensor that is slow or biased can make a good converter appear inefficient.

causes.title: Skewed upstream A/F sensor
causes.description: A skewed upstream sensor keeps the mixture off target, reducing converter efficiency and test results.

causes.title: Exhaust leak ahead of the downstream sensor
causes.description: Outside air entering near the downstream sensor makes it read lean and switch, mimicking a failed converter.

causes.title: Underlying misfire or fuel control problem
causes.description: Misfire or a persistent rich or lean mixture overloads the converter and lowers its measured efficiency; it must be fixed before replacing the converter.

modifiers.reason: Misfire or fuel trim code present

causes.title: Oil or coolant consumption contaminating the converter
causes.description: Burning oil or coolant coats the converter and sensors and will destroy a replacement converter.

causes.title: Non-compliant or incorrect replacement converter
causes.description: A replacement converter not certified for the vehicle may lack enough oxygen storage to pass the monitor.

causes.title: PCM calibration requiring an update
causes.description: Catalyst monitor calibrations have been revised on some vehicles to correct false failures.

causes.title: Downstream sensor wiring or connector fault
causes.description: Damaged sensor wiring distorts the downstream signal the monitor relies on.

modifiers.reason: Recent exhaust work or wiring damage

tests.title: Review related codes, trims, and misfire history
tests.purpose: Make sure the engine is running correctly before judging the converter.
procedure: Record all codes and freeze frames, including pending and history codes.
Check misfire counters and Mode $06 misfire data on all cylinders.
Record fuel trims per bank at idle and cruise.
Ask about oil or coolant consumption and recent exhaust work.
tests.expected: No other codes, no misfire, and fuel trims near zero (general guideline: total within roughly ±10% (general guideline — verify against OEM specification)).

outcomes.label: Misfire, fuel trim, or sensor faults also present
outcomes.interpretation: Repair the other faults first, then re-run the catalyst monitor.

outcomes.label: Only the catalyst code; engine running correctly
outcomes.interpretation: Continue with sensor, exhaust leak, and converter tests.

outcomes.label: History unknown or codes cleared recently
outcomes.interpretation: No change; road test and recheck.

tests.title: Upstream O2 / A/F sensor response test (induced rich and lean)
tests.purpose: Determine whether the upstream oxygen or air/fuel ratio sensor reports mixture changes accurately and quickly, separating a sensor fault from a true lean or rich condition.
procedure: Identify the upstream sensor type (narrowband zirconia O2 or wideband A/F) from service information; this changes how the data is read.
Warm the engine to full operating temperature and confirm closed-loop operation. Check for exhaust leaks ahead of the sensor first; a leak invalidates this test.
Graph the upstream sensor signal (voltage, current, or lambda/equivalence ratio PID) for each bank at idle and at a steady elevated engine speed.
Induce a rich condition (a brief snap of the throttle, or a controlled amount of propane at the intake) and observe how quickly the sensor reports rich.
Induce a lean condition (a brief deceleration with fuel cut, or a controlled vacuum leak) and observe how quickly the sensor reports lean.
Compare the responses between banks and with the fuel trims; the sensor should track every mixture change promptly.
tests.expected: The sensor follows each induced rich and lean change quickly and fully, and both banks behave alike (response time per OEM specification; a narrowband sensor generally swings well above and below its midpoint (general guideline — verify against OEM specification)).

outcomes.label: Sensor responds quickly and fully to induced rich and lean changes
outcomes.interpretation: The sensor is reporting accurately; any lean or rich reading reflects the actual mixture, so look for the underlying cause.

outcomes.label: Response is slow, reduced in amplitude, or noticeably worse than the other bank
outcomes.interpretation: The sensor is aged or contaminated. Check the heater and look for contamination sources before replacing it.

outcomes.label: Sensor stays biased lean or rich, or does not respond to an induced change
outcomes.interpretation: The signal is not believable. Test the signal and heater circuits before condemning the sensor.

outcomes.label: Exhaust leak present or closed loop could not be achieved
outcomes.interpretation: No change; repair any exhaust leak ahead of the sensor or resolve the open-loop cause, then repeat.

tests.title: Compare upstream and downstream sensor activity
tests.purpose: Judge converter oxygen storage by how much the downstream signal mirrors the upstream signal.
procedure: Warm the engine and converter fully (drive for several minutes).
Graph upstream and downstream sensors together at a steady elevated engine speed.
An efficient converter normally leaves the downstream signal steady while the upstream signal switches or varies.
Snap the throttle and decelerate to confirm the downstream sensor can reach both rich and lean.
tests.expected: Downstream signal steady and much less active than the upstream signal, and able to reach rich and lean when forced.

outcomes.label: Downstream steady and responds when forced
outcomes.interpretation: The converter appears to be storing oxygen; review the monitor data and software.

outcomes.label: Downstream closely mirrors the upstream switching
outcomes.interpretation: Low oxygen storage; confirm there are no exhaust leaks or contamination sources before replacing the converter.

outcomes.label: Downstream biased lean, erratic, or unresponsive
outcomes.interpretation: Suspect an exhaust leak near the sensor, the sensor, or its wiring.

outcomes.label: Could not reach full operating temperature
outcomes.interpretation: No change; repeat after a longer drive.

tests.title: Inspect for exhaust leaks ahead of the downstream sensor
tests.purpose: Rule out outside air fooling the downstream sensor.
procedure: With the engine cold, start it and listen for leaks from the manifold back to the downstream sensor.
Engine off and cool: inspect joints, flex pipe, flanges, and sensor bosses for soot trails and cracks.
Optionally introduce low-pressure smoke into the tailpipe with the engine off.
tests.expected: No leaks between the engine and the downstream sensor.

outcomes.label: No leaks found
outcomes.interpretation: Exhaust leaks are not the cause.

outcomes.label: Leak found ahead of the downstream sensor
outcomes.interpretation: Repair the leak and re-run the catalyst monitor before replacing the converter.

outcomes.label: Could not inspect the full system
outcomes.interpretation: No change.

tests.title: Review Mode $06 catalyst monitor results
tests.purpose: Quantify how far the converter test result is from its threshold.
procedure: Complete the catalyst monitor drive cycle per service information.
Read Mode $06 catalyst test values and limits for each bank.
Compare the result with the threshold and between banks.
tests.expected: Catalyst test results within limits on each bank.

outcomes.label: Results within limits
outcomes.interpretation: The converter currently passes; review conditions under which the code set and consider software updates.

outcomes.label: Marginal failure, close to the threshold
outcomes.interpretation: Check leaks, sensors, and software before condemning the converter.

outcomes.label: Clear failure, far past the threshold
outcomes.interpretation: A converter fault is likely once engine, sensor, and leak causes are ruled out.

outcomes.label: Monitor did not complete
outcomes.interpretation: No change; follow the OEM drive cycle.

tests.title: Check for oil or coolant consumption
tests.purpose: Find contamination sources that would damage a replacement converter.
procedure: Review oil top-up and coolant top-up history.
Look for blue or white exhaust smoke, oil-wet tailpipe deposits, and a sweet exhaust odor.
Pressure test the cooling system and perform a combustion gas (block) test if coolant loss is suspected.
Inspect spark plugs for oil or coolant deposits.
tests.expected: No oil or coolant consumption and no contamination on plugs.

outcomes.label: No oil or coolant consumption found
outcomes.interpretation: No contamination source; a replacement converter should not be at risk.

outcomes.label: Oil or coolant consumption confirmed
outcomes.interpretation: Repair the source of oil or coolant consumption before any converter replacement.

outcomes.label: History not available
outcomes.interpretation: No change.

tests.title: Verify the converter is the correct certified part
tests.purpose: Rule out a non-compliant replacement converter.
procedure: Check whether the converter has been replaced and inspect its labeling.
Confirm the part is certified for this vehicle and emissions certification (for example, CARB-compliant where required).
Check for any missing or modified components such as removed converters or sensor spacers.
tests.expected: Original or correctly certified converter installed with no modifications.

outcomes.label: Correct converter installed
outcomes.interpretation: The converter type is correct.

outcomes.label: Non-compliant, incorrect, or modified converter found
outcomes.interpretation: Install a correctly certified converter; do not use sensor spacers or other defeat devices.

outcomes.label: Could not determine
outcomes.interpretation: No change.

tests.title: Test the downstream sensor circuit
tests.purpose: Rule out wiring or connector faults distorting the downstream signal.
procedure: Key off: inspect the downstream harness for melting, chafing, and correct routing; inspect the connector for corrosion.
Key on, sensor unplugged: check PCM bias voltage on the signal circuit and continuity of the signal and ground circuits.
Wiggle the harness while graphing the signal with the sensor connected.
tests.expected: Correct bias voltage, no opens or shorts, and a stable signal during the wiggle test.

outcomes.label: Circuit good
outcomes.interpretation: Wiring is not the cause.

outcomes.label: Wiring or connector fault found
outcomes.interpretation: Repair the wiring and re-run the catalyst monitor.

outcomes.label: Could not access the circuit
outcomes.interpretation: No change.

tests.title: Check technical service bulletins and PCM software level
tests.purpose: Identify known pattern failures, revised parts, or calibration updates for catalyst efficiency monitoring.
procedure: Search OEM service information for bulletins, campaigns, and recalls that match the codes and symptoms for this vehicle.
Read the current PCM calibration ID with a scan tool and compare it with the latest available calibration.
Note any bulletin-directed diagnostic steps or revised parts before continuing.
tools: Scan tool with calibration ID readout
tests.expected: No applicable bulletin and the PCM calibration is current.

outcomes.label: No applicable bulletin; calibration current
outcomes.interpretation: Software and known pattern failures are unlikely; continue with testing.

outcomes.label: Applicable bulletin or calibration update found
outcomes.interpretation: Follow the bulletin procedure, then verify the repair before replacing other parts.

outcomes.label: Service information not available
outcomes.interpretation: No change; continue with direct testing.

verification: Clear codes after confirming the repair.
Complete the catalyst monitor drive cycle per service information.
Confirm Mode $06 catalyst results are within limits for each bank.
Confirm no misfire, fuel trim, or sensor codes are present.

playbooks.title: MAF / MAP sensor circuit and performance
playbooks.summary: Airflow and manifold pressure codes divide into circuit faults (a signal fixed at zero, default, or rail value) and range/performance or correlation faults (an active signal that disagrees with the PCM's model). Circuit faults call for power, ground, reference, and signal testing. Performance faults are often caused by contamination, air leaks after the MAF or after the throttle, a leaking MAP hose, or restrictions in the intake or exhaust, rather than by the sensor itself. Compare readings with independent measurements before replacing a sensor.
clarifyingQuestions: Which codes are set: circuit low/high, or range/performance/correlation?
Has the air filter or intake been serviced recently, or is an oiled or aftermarket filter installed?
Is there a hissing noise, high idle, or low power?
Are there reference voltage codes or other sensor codes at the same time?
Is the MAP sensor remote-mounted with a hose, or mounted on the manifold?

causes.title: Contaminated MAF sensing element
causes.description: Dust or oil on the hot-wire or hot-film element makes the sensor under-report airflow, setting range/performance codes and lean trims.

modifiers.reason: Oiled or aftermarket filter or dusty conditions

causes.title: Failed MAF sensor
causes.description: An internal sensor fault produces an erratic, fixed, or skewed signal.

causes.title: MAF power, ground, or signal circuit fault
causes.description: A missing supply or ground, or an open or shorted signal wire, sets MAF circuit codes.

causes.title: Failed or skewed MAP sensor
causes.description: An internal fault or contamination makes the MAP reading disagree with actual manifold pressure.

causes.title: Leaking, kinked, or plugged MAP sensor hose or port
causes.description: A remote-mounted MAP sensor reads incorrectly if its hose leaks, kinks, or fills with oil or carbon.

causes.title: Air leak between the MAF and the throttle body
causes.description: Air bypassing the MAF makes measured airflow lower than actual, setting MAF performance and correlation codes.

modifiers.reason: Recent air filter or intake work

causes.title: Vacuum leak after the throttle
causes.description: A large leak raises manifold pressure and airflow relative to throttle position, causing MAP/MAF/TP correlation faults.

causes.title: Restricted air filter or inlet
causes.description: A plugged filter or blocked inlet reduces airflow at high load, making MAF readings lower than the PCM expects.

causes.title: Exhaust restriction affecting manifold pressure
causes.description: A restricted exhaust keeps manifold pressure high, so MAP and calculated airflow disagree with the PCM model.

causes.title: Shared 5-volt reference circuit pulled down or open
causes.description: The MAP sensor usually shares a 5-volt reference with other sensors; a short in any of them affects all.

causes.title: Sensor signal or ground wiring damage
causes.description: Chafed or broken signal and ground wires cause intermittent or fixed readings.

causes.title: PCM calibration requiring an update
causes.description: Some airflow rationality monitors have been revised by calibration updates.

tests.title: Review codes and key-on / idle sensor data
tests.purpose: Separate circuit faults from range/performance faults and check basic plausibility.
procedure: Record all codes and freeze frames, including reference voltage codes.
Key on, engine off: MAF should read near zero airflow and MAP should match BARO.
At warm idle, record MAF, MAP, TP, calculated load, and fuel trims.
Graph the sensors during a snap throttle and note dropouts or fixed values.
tests.expected: Readings plausible at key-on and idle, and responsive during a snap throttle (values per OEM specification).

outcomes.label: A sensor is fixed at a default, zero, or rail value
outcomes.interpretation: A circuit fault is likely; test power, ground, reference, and signal circuits.

outcomes.label: Sensors active but readings implausible or disagree
outcomes.interpretation: Check for leaks, restrictions, and contamination, and compare with independent measurements.

outcomes.label: All readings currently plausible
outcomes.interpretation: The fault may be intermittent or load-dependent; test under load and wiggle-test the harness.

outcomes.label: Sensor PIDs not available
outcomes.interpretation: No change.

tests.title: Compare the MAP PID with a vacuum gauge and barometric pressure
tests.purpose: Verify the MAP sensor reading against an independent gauge and use the vacuum pattern to spot leaks and exhaust restriction.
procedure: Key on, engine off: compare the MAP and BARO PIDs; both should indicate current atmospheric pressure.
Tee a vacuum gauge (or a pressure transducer on a lab scope) into a manifold vacuum source close to the MAP sensor port.
Start the engine and compare gauge vacuum with the MAP PID at warm idle, converting units as needed.
Hold a steady elevated engine speed (for example about 2,500 rpm) for up to a minute and watch whether vacuum stays steady or slowly falls.
Snap the throttle and note how quickly MAP and the gauge respond and recover.
tools: Vacuum gauge or pressure transducer with lab scope
tests.expected: MAP PID matches the gauge and BARO at key-on, idle vacuum is steady, and vacuum holds or rises slightly at a sustained elevated speed (normal values per OEM specification and altitude (general guideline — verify against OEM specification)).

outcomes.label: MAP agrees with the gauge and the vacuum pattern is normal
outcomes.interpretation: MAP sensing and basic engine breathing are normal; focus on other causes.

outcomes.label: MAP PID disagrees with the gauge or with BARO at key-on
outcomes.interpretation: The MAP sensor, its hose, or its circuit is skewed; test the circuit before replacing the sensor.

outcomes.label: MAP and gauge agree, but idle vacuum is low or unsteady
outcomes.interpretation: Suggests an intake leak, retarded valve timing, or a mechanical fault; smoke test the intake and verify timing.

outcomes.label: Vacuum falls steadily at a sustained elevated speed or recovers slowly after a snap
outcomes.interpretation: Classic sign of exhaust restriction; confirm with a back-pressure test.

outcomes.label: No suitable manifold vacuum port available
outcomes.interpretation: No change; use the MAP PID with a pressure transducer or other tests.

tests.title: Check MAF readings at idle and wide-open throttle
tests.purpose: Verify the MAF reports airflow consistent with the engine size and speed.
procedure: At warm idle, compare MAF with the expected value (general guideline: roughly equal in grams per second to engine displacement in liters (general guideline — verify against OEM specification)).
During a safe wide-open-throttle acceleration, record peak MAF, rpm, and throttle position; compare with the OEM specification or known-good data.
Watch for dropouts, spikes, or a flat reading as airflow increases.
Where the PCM allows, unplug the MAF briefly at idle and note whether fuel trims improve.
tests.expected: MAF readings rise smoothly with airflow and reach expected values (per OEM specification or known-good data).

outcomes.label: MAF plausible at idle and under load
outcomes.interpretation: The MAF signal is believable.

outcomes.label: MAF low, especially under load
outcomes.interpretation: Inspect the element, check for air leaks after the MAF, and inspect the filter.

outcomes.label: MAF erratic, spiking, or high
outcomes.interpretation: Check the MAF circuit and connector, then consider the sensor.

outcomes.label: Loaded test could not be performed safely
outcomes.interpretation: No change.

tests.title: Inspect the MAF element and housing
tests.purpose: Look for contamination or damage on the sensing element.
procedure: Key off: remove the MAF per the OEM procedure without touching the element.
Inspect the element and screen for dust, oil, debris, or damage.
Clean with a MAF-safe cleaner only if the OEM permits, allow to dry fully, and reinstall.
Re-check MAF readings after cleaning.
tests.expected: Element and screen clean and undamaged.

outcomes.label: Element clean and undamaged
outcomes.interpretation: Contamination is not the cause.

outcomes.label: Dust, oil, or debris on the element
outcomes.interpretation: Correct the source (filter fit, oiled filter, PCV oil) and clean or replace, then retest.

outcomes.label: Element broken or visibly damaged
outcomes.interpretation: Replace the MAF sensor.

outcomes.label: Sensor is integral and cannot be inspected
outcomes.interpretation: No change.

tests.title: Test MAF power, ground, and signal circuits
tests.purpose: Confirm the MAF is properly powered and its signal reaches the PCM.
procedure: Back-probe the MAF connector with the key on and engine running.
Measure supply voltage and ground voltage drop against the battery.
Check the signal (voltage or frequency, per design) at the sensor and at the PCM and compare.
Wiggle the harness while graphing the signal.
tests.expected: Supply and ground within the OEM limits and the same signal at the sensor and the PCM.

outcomes.label: Power, ground, and signal path good
outcomes.interpretation: The circuit is good; a fixed or erratic signal points to the sensor.

outcomes.label: Supply or ground missing or excessive voltage drop
outcomes.interpretation: Repair the power or ground circuit and retest.

outcomes.label: Signal differs between the sensor and the PCM or drops out when wiggled
outcomes.interpretation: Repair the signal wiring or connector.

outcomes.label: Could not access the circuits
outcomes.interpretation: No change.

tests.title: Test MAP reference, signal, and ground circuits
tests.purpose: Confirm the MAP sensor has a good 5-volt reference and ground and that its signal reaches the PCM.
procedure: Back-probe the MAP connector with the key on.
Measure the 5-volt reference and ground voltage drop.
If the reference is low, unplug other sensors on the same reference one at a time and see whether it recovers.
Compare the signal at the sensor and at the PCM and wiggle-test the harness.
tests.expected: Reference and ground within the OEM specification and the same signal at the sensor and the PCM.

outcomes.label: Reference, ground, and signal path good
outcomes.interpretation: The circuit is good.

outcomes.label: Reference low or missing
outcomes.interpretation: Find the sensor or wire pulling the reference down; replace the shorted component.

outcomes.label: Signal or ground circuit open, shorted, or intermittent
outcomes.interpretation: Repair the wiring or connector.

outcomes.label: Could not access the circuits
outcomes.interpretation: No change.

tests.title: Inspect the MAP sensor hose and port
tests.purpose: Rule out a leaking, kinked, or plugged sensing path.
procedure: Key off: inspect the MAP hose (if remote-mounted) for cracks, kinks, collapse, and loose fittings.
Remove the sensor and inspect the port and sensor inlet for oil, carbon, or ice.
Apply vacuum to the sensor with a hand pump and confirm the PID changes smoothly and holds.
tests.expected: Hose and port clear and sealed; sensor responds smoothly to applied vacuum.

outcomes.label: Hose and port clear; sensor tracks applied vacuum
outcomes.interpretation: The sensing path and sensor respond correctly.

outcomes.label: Hose leaking or kinked, or port plugged
outcomes.interpretation: Repair the hose or clean the port and retest.

outcomes.label: Path good, but the PID does not track applied vacuum
outcomes.interpretation: Replace the MAP sensor after confirming its circuit is good.

outcomes.label: Sensor mounted directly to the manifold with no hose
outcomes.interpretation: No change; inspect the port only.

tests.title: Smoke test the intake from the air filter to the manifold
tests.purpose: Find air leaking into the intake after the MAF or after the throttle.
procedure: Engine off. Seal the intake at the air filter housing per the smoke machine instructions.
Introduce smoke and inspect the duct and couplers, throttle body and intake gaskets, vacuum hoses, and PCV connections.
Remove the equipment and reconnect everything.
tests.expected: No smoke escapes anywhere in the intake.

outcomes.label: No smoke escapes
outcomes.interpretation: Air leaks are not the cause.

outcomes.label: Smoke between the MAF and the throttle body
outcomes.interpretation: Replace the duct or coupler and retest.

outcomes.label: Smoke at a vacuum hose or gasket after the throttle
outcomes.interpretation: Repair the leak and retest.

outcomes.label: Could not seal the intake
outcomes.interpretation: No change.

tests.title: Inspect the air filter and inlet
tests.purpose: Rule out an intake restriction or an oiled filter contaminating the MAF.
procedure: Engine off: remove the air filter and inspect for heavy dirt, water, excess oil (oiled filters), or incorrect fit.
Inspect the inlet snorkel and duct for debris, nests, snow, or collapse.
Optionally measure intake restriction at wide-open throttle and compare with the OEM specification.
tests.expected: Correct, clean filter properly seated with a clear inlet.

outcomes.label: Filter and inlet good
outcomes.interpretation: The filter and inlet are not the cause.

outcomes.label: Filter plugged or inlet obstructed
outcomes.interpretation: Replace the filter or clear the obstruction and retest.

outcomes.label: Over-oiled filter or poorly fitted filter letting dirt past
outcomes.interpretation: Correct the filter, then clean or replace the MAF as needed.

outcomes.label: Not inspected
outcomes.interpretation: No change.

tests.title: Check technical service bulletins and PCM software level
tests.purpose: Identify known pattern failures, revised parts, or calibration updates for MAF and MAP rationality monitors.
procedure: Search OEM service information for bulletins, campaigns, and recalls that match the codes and symptoms for this vehicle.
Read the current PCM calibration ID with a scan tool and compare it with the latest available calibration.
Note any bulletin-directed diagnostic steps or revised parts before continuing.
tools: Scan tool with calibration ID readout
tests.expected: No applicable bulletin and the PCM calibration is current.

outcomes.label: No applicable bulletin; calibration current
outcomes.interpretation: Software and known pattern failures are unlikely; continue with testing.

outcomes.label: Applicable bulletin or calibration update found
outcomes.interpretation: Follow the bulletin procedure, then verify the repair before replacing other parts.

outcomes.label: Service information not available
outcomes.interpretation: No change; continue with direct testing.

verification: Clear codes after recording the freeze frame.
Confirm key-on MAF near zero and MAP equal to BARO, and plausible readings at idle and under load.
Confirm fuel trims near zero (general guideline: total within roughly ±10% (general guideline — verify against OEM specification)).
Complete a drive cycle and confirm no airflow or pressure codes return.

playbooks.title: Coolant temperature, thermostat, and intake air temperature
playbooks.summary: Temperature sensor codes are either circuit faults (a reading fixed at the extreme cold or hot end, usually wiring or connectors) or plausibility and warm-up faults (a reading that is active but wrong, or an engine that warms too slowly). P0128 and P0125 are most often a thermostat that opens early, but low coolant, trapped air, a fan that runs continuously, a skewed ECT sensor, or extreme cold can also cause them. Use the unplug/jumper circuit test for extreme readings, and compare ECT and IAT with independent temperatures before replacing a sensor.
clarifyingQuestions: Does the temperature gauge reach its normal position, and does the heater get hot?
Is the reading stuck at an extreme, erratic, or just slow to rise?
Was the cooling system recently serviced, or is coolant being lost?
Does the cooling fan run on a cold engine?
What was the ambient temperature and trip length when the code set?

causes.title: Failed or skewed coolant temperature sensor
causes.description: A sensor whose resistance has drifted reports the wrong temperature, affecting fueling, fan control, and warm-up monitors.

causes.title: Thermostat stuck open or opening early
causes.description: Coolant flows through the radiator too soon, so the engine warms slowly or never reaches the temperature the PCM expects.

modifiers.reason: Poor heat or low gauge reading

causes.title: Failed or skewed intake air temperature sensor
causes.description: An IAT sensor that reads incorrectly affects fueling and makes ECT/IAT plausibility checks fail.

causes.title: Sensor signal or return wiring open or shorted
causes.description: An open signal wire makes a thermistor read extremely cold; a short to ground makes it read extremely hot.

causes.title: Corroded or loose sensor connector
causes.description: Corrosion or loose terminals add resistance, so the sensor reads colder than actual or jumps erratically.

modifiers.reason: Erratic reading or coolant on the connector

causes.title: Air pocket at the ECT sensor
causes.description: Trapped air around the sensor makes it read low or erratic until the system is bled.

causes.title: Low coolant level
causes.description: With coolant below the sensor, the sensor reads air temperature rather than coolant temperature.

causes.title: Cooling fan running when it should be off
causes.description: A fan relay stuck on or a fan commanded on by a faulty input pulls heat away and slows warm-up.

causes.title: Extreme cold ambient or very short trips
causes.description: Very low ambient temperatures, high-speed cold airflow, or very short trips can prevent warm-up within the monitor's time window without any fault.

causes.title: PCM calibration requiring an update
causes.description: Warm-up and thermostat monitor calibrations have been revised on some vehicles.

tests.title: Review codes and temperature PIDs
tests.purpose: Separate circuit faults (implausible extreme readings) from warm-up performance faults.
procedure: Record all codes and freeze frames, including ECT, IAT, ambient, and run time.
Key on: note ECT and IAT readings; readings at the extreme cold or extreme hot end of the scale point to a circuit fault.
Start the engine and graph ECT and IAT; watch for jumps or dropouts.
tests.expected: ECT and IAT readings plausible and changing smoothly.

outcomes.label: ECT or IAT fixed at an extreme cold or hot value
outcomes.interpretation: A circuit fault is likely; perform the circuit test.

outcomes.label: Readings jump or drop out
outcomes.interpretation: Check coolant level and trapped air, and inspect the connector.

outcomes.label: Readings plausible but warm-up slow or incomplete
outcomes.interpretation: Verify ECT accuracy and thermostat operation.

outcomes.label: Could not observe a full warm-up
outcomes.interpretation: No change.

tests.title: ECT plausibility: cold-soak comparison and warm-up curve
tests.purpose: Confirm that the coolant temperature sensor reads the actual engine temperature and that the engine warms up normally.
procedure: After a cold soak (engine off for several hours), compare ECT, IAT, and ambient temperature PIDs; they should be close to each other.
Start the engine and graph ECT during warm-up at idle and then at a steady speed, noting the time to reach normal operating temperature.
Measure the actual temperature at the thermostat housing or near the ECT sensor with an infrared or contact thermometer and compare it with the PID.
Feel or measure the upper radiator hose; it should stay cool until the thermostat opens, then warm quickly.
tests.expected: ECT agrees with the other temperature PIDs after a cold soak, tracks the measured temperature, and reaches normal operating temperature within the expected time (warm-up time and thermostat opening temperature per OEM specification).

outcomes.label: ECT is plausible and warm-up is normal
outcomes.interpretation: Coolant temperature sensing and thermostat control are normal.

outcomes.label: ECT PID disagrees with the cold-soak temperatures or with the measured temperature
outcomes.interpretation: The ECT sensor or its circuit is skewed; check the circuit and connector before replacing the sensor.

outcomes.label: ECT is accurate, but the engine warms slowly or never reaches operating temperature; upper hose warms early
outcomes.interpretation: The thermostat is opening early or stuck open.

outcomes.label: Could not cold soak or observe a full warm-up
outcomes.interpretation: No change; repeat after the vehicle sits overnight.

tests.title: Check coolant level and bleed trapped air
tests.purpose: Make sure the ECT sensor is surrounded by coolant.
procedure: With the engine fully cool, check the coolant level in the reservoir and, where accessible, at the radiator; never open a hot, pressurized system.
Inspect for external leaks.
If the level is low or the system was recently serviced, fill and bleed per the OEM procedure (bleeder screws or vacuum fill).
Recheck the ECT reading and warm-up curve.
tools: Vacuum fill tool or bleeding funnel
tests.expected: Coolant at the correct level with no air in the system.

outcomes.label: Coolant full with no air
outcomes.interpretation: Coolant level is not the cause.

outcomes.label: Coolant level low
outcomes.interpretation: Refill, find and repair the leak, and recheck the reading.

outcomes.label: Level correct but air bled out and the reading stabilized
outcomes.interpretation: Air was the cause; confirm the system stays full after several heat cycles.

outcomes.label: Engine too hot to open the system safely
outcomes.interpretation: No change; recheck when cool.

tests.title: Test the temperature sensor circuit with the unplug/jumper method
tests.purpose: Determine whether a circuit or the sensor is causing an extreme or erratic reading.
procedure: Key on: unplug the sensor; the PID should go to the extreme cold end of the scale (open circuit).
Install a fused jumper across the harness terminals; the PID should go to the extreme hot end (short circuit).
If the PID responds correctly, the wiring and PCM are good and the sensor is suspect.
If it does not respond, measure the reference (bias) voltage and return circuit at the connector and trace the wiring.
tests.expected: PID moves to the extreme cold end when unplugged and the extreme hot end when jumpered.

outcomes.label: PID responds correctly; circuit good
outcomes.interpretation: The circuit is good; the sensor is suspect if readings are wrong.

outcomes.label: PID does not respond or bias voltage is missing
outcomes.interpretation: Repair the open or shorted wiring and retest.

outcomes.label: Terminals corroded, loose, or coolant in the connector
outcomes.interpretation: Repair the terminals; coolant in the connector can mean a leaking sensor, which must be replaced.

outcomes.label: Could not access the sensor connector
outcomes.interpretation: No change.

tests.title: Measure ECT and IAT sensor resistance against temperature
tests.purpose: Confirm whether the sensor element matches its temperature curve.
procedure: Key off: unplug the sensor and measure resistance across its terminals.
Measure the actual temperature at the same time (thermometer in the coolant or near the IAT).
Compare with the OEM resistance-versus-temperature table.
Repeat at a second temperature if possible.
tests.expected: Resistance matches the OEM table at the measured temperatures.

outcomes.label: Both sensors match the table
outcomes.interpretation: Sensor elements are accurate.

outcomes.label: ECT resistance out of specification
outcomes.interpretation: Replace the ECT sensor and bleed the cooling system afterwards.

outcomes.label: IAT resistance out of specification
outcomes.interpretation: Replace the IAT sensor (or the MAF assembly if the IAT is integrated).

outcomes.label: No specification available
outcomes.interpretation: No change; use the plausibility comparison instead.

tests.title: Compare IAT with ambient and ECT
tests.purpose: Confirm the IAT reads correctly after a cold soak and while driving.
procedure: After a cold soak, compare IAT with ECT and the ambient temperature PID or a thermometer.
Drive at steady speed and confirm IAT stays near ambient (turbo engines: near charge-air temperature).
Note whether the IAT is a separate sensor or integrated into the MAF.
tests.expected: IAT close to ambient after a cold soak and during steady driving (general guideline: within a few degrees (general guideline — verify against OEM specification)).

outcomes.label: IAT plausible
outcomes.interpretation: The IAT is accurate.

outcomes.label: IAT fixed, skewed, or unrelated to ambient
outcomes.interpretation: Check the circuit, then replace the sensor if the circuit is good.

outcomes.label: Could not cold soak
outcomes.interpretation: No change.

tests.title: Check that the cooling fan is off during warm-up
tests.purpose: Rule out a fan running continuously and slowing warm-up.
procedure: Start a cold engine with the A/C off and observe the cooling fan.
Check the fan command PID and relay or module output.
Keep hands, clothing, and tools away from the fan; it can start at any time.
tests.expected: Fan off during a cold warm-up with the A/C off (fan strategy per OEM specification).

outcomes.label: Fan off during warm-up
outcomes.interpretation: The fan is not the cause.

outcomes.label: Fan runs continuously on a cold engine
outcomes.interpretation: Find why: stuck relay, fan module fault, or an input commanding the fan (such as ECT reading hot).

outcomes.label: Could not observe
outcomes.interpretation: No change.

tests.title: Review operating conditions when the code set
tests.purpose: Determine whether extreme cold or short trips explain a warm-up code without a fault.
procedure: Review the freeze frame ambient temperature, IAT, and engine run time.
Ask about short trips, extended idling, and aftermarket grille covers or winter fronts.
Compare with the monitor enable criteria in service information.
tests.expected: Code set under normal ambient conditions and trip length.

outcomes.label: Code set in normal conditions
outcomes.interpretation: Operating conditions do not explain the code.

outcomes.label: Code set in extreme cold or during very short trips
outcomes.interpretation: Retest in normal conditions; the thermostat may still be marginal.

outcomes.label: No freeze frame available
outcomes.interpretation: No change.

tests.title: Check technical service bulletins and PCM software level
tests.purpose: Identify known pattern failures, revised parts, or calibration updates for coolant temperature and thermostat monitors.
procedure: Search OEM service information for bulletins, campaigns, and recalls that match the codes and symptoms for this vehicle.
Read the current PCM calibration ID with a scan tool and compare it with the latest available calibration.
Note any bulletin-directed diagnostic steps or revised parts before continuing.
tools: Scan tool with calibration ID readout
tests.expected: No applicable bulletin and the PCM calibration is current.

outcomes.label: No applicable bulletin; calibration current
outcomes.interpretation: Software and known pattern failures are unlikely; continue with testing.

outcomes.label: Applicable bulletin or calibration update found
outcomes.interpretation: Follow the bulletin procedure, then verify the repair before replacing other parts.

outcomes.label: Service information not available
outcomes.interpretation: No change; continue with direct testing.

verification: Clear codes after recording the freeze frame.
Cold soak, then confirm ECT, IAT, and ambient agree before start-up.
Confirm the engine reaches normal operating temperature within the expected time and the heater output is normal.
Complete a drive cycle and confirm the thermostat and temperature sensor monitors pass.

playbooks.title: Crank / cam sensor signals and correlation
playbooks.summary: Crankshaft and camshaft position codes are either signal faults (a weak, noisy, or missing sensor signal) or correlation faults (clean signals that are out of their expected relationship). Signal faults are usually a sensor, its wiring or connector, a pulled-down reference, or a poorly seated or incorrect replacement sensor. Correlation faults (P0016-P0019) usually mean a stretched timing chain, a jumped belt or chain, a phaser that does not park, low or incorrect oil, or a shifted target wheel. Scoping crank and cam signals together against a known-good pattern separates the two branches quickly; verify mechanical timing before replacing timing components.
clarifyingQuestions: Are the codes for a sensor circuit or for cam/crank correlation, and which bank?
Is there a rattle on start-up or any change in engine noise?
What is the oil maintenance history and current oil level?
Has any timing, sensor, flywheel, or balancer work been done recently?
Does the engine stall or crank long, especially when hot?

causes.title: Failed crankshaft position sensor
causes.description: An internal sensor fault produces a weak, noisy, or missing crank signal, often worse when hot.

causes.title: Failed camshaft position sensor
causes.description: A failing cam sensor gives an intermittent or distorted signal, causing sync loss, long crank, or correlation faults.

causes.title: Damaged or shifted crank or cam target wheel
causes.description: Bent, missing, or shifted teeth on a target wheel distort the signal pattern and the cam/crank relationship.

modifiers.reason: Recent work near a target wheel

causes.title: Stretched timing chain or worn guides and tensioner
causes.description: Chain wear lets the camshafts fall behind the crankshaft, setting correlation codes on one or both banks.

causes.title: Timing belt or chain jumped a tooth
causes.description: A jumped belt or chain puts the cams out of phase by a fixed amount, usually with a sudden onset of poor running.

modifiers.reason: Sudden onset or recent belt work

causes.title: Cam phaser not returning to its park position
causes.description: A worn or sticking phaser, or a failed lock pin, leaves the cam out of its expected park position at idle.

modifiers.match: knock at start|clatter at start|rattle for a few seconds

causes.title: Low oil level or pressure affecting cam phasing
causes.description: Phasers and hydraulic tensioners need oil pressure; low oil lets the chain slap and the cam timing drift.

causes.title: Crank or cam sensor wiring damage
causes.description: Chafed, broken, or poorly routed wiring, often near ignition components, causes dropouts and noise.

causes.title: Corroded or oil-soaked sensor connector
causes.description: Oil wicking through a leaking sensor seal or corrosion at the connector disturbs the low-level signal.

causes.title: Shared sensor reference circuit pulled down or open
causes.description: Hall-effect sensors often share a 5-volt reference; a short in another sensor on the same reference disables them.

causes.title: Sensor not seated correctly or incorrect replacement sensor
causes.description: An incorrect air gap, a sensor that is not fully seated, or a non-matching replacement sensor produces a weak or distorted signal.

causes.title: PCM calibration requiring an update
causes.description: Some correlation and sensor monitors have been revised by calibration updates.

tests.title: Review codes, sync status, and cam/crank data
tests.purpose: Separate sensor signal faults from true timing correlation faults.
procedure: Record all codes and freeze frames, including reference voltage codes.
Check the rpm PID while cranking and the cam/crank sync status where available.
At warm idle, record cam position deviation or correlation PIDs for each camshaft with the phasers at park.
Note whether codes point to one sensor or to correlation on one or both banks.
tests.expected: No signal dropouts and cam/crank correlation within the OEM specification.

outcomes.label: Sensor circuit codes, rpm dropouts, or sync loss
outcomes.interpretation: Scope the signals and test the sensor circuits.

outcomes.label: Correlation codes with signals present and clean
outcomes.interpretation: Focus on mechanical timing, phaser park position, and oil supply.

outcomes.label: Codes intermittent and not currently active
outcomes.interpretation: No change; capture data during the fault.

tests.title: Scope crank and cam signals together
tests.purpose: Check signal quality and the cam-to-crank relationship against a known-good pattern.
procedure: Back-probe the crank and cam signal wires and capture them together at cranking and idle.
Check each signal for amplitude, clean edges, noise, and dropouts; heat or wiggle the harness if the fault is intermittent.
Compare the cam edge positions relative to the crank missing-tooth gap with a known-good pattern for this engine.
Repeat for each camshaft.
tools: Lab scope with at least two channels
tests.expected: Clean signals with the cam edges in the same position relative to the crank as the known-good pattern.

outcomes.label: Signals clean and relationship matches known-good
outcomes.interpretation: Sensors and timing are correct at the time of the test; consider intermittent or software causes.

outcomes.label: A signal is weak, noisy, missing, or drops out
outcomes.interpretation: Test the sensor circuit before replacing the sensor.

outcomes.label: Signal clean but tooth pattern distorted or missing teeth
outcomes.interpretation: Inspect the target wheel for damage or debris.

outcomes.label: Signals clean but the cam/crank relationship is shifted
outcomes.interpretation: Verify phaser park position and oil supply, then verify mechanical timing.

outcomes.label: No known-good pattern available
outcomes.interpretation: No change; use OEM correlation PIDs instead.

tests.title: Test crank and cam sensor power, ground, and signal circuits
tests.purpose: Find wiring, connector, or reference faults before replacing a sensor.
procedure: Key on: back-probe the sensor connector and measure the reference or supply voltage and ground voltage drop.
If the reference is low, unplug sensors on the same reference one at a time and watch for recovery.
Check the signal wire for continuity to the PCM and for shorts to ground or voltage.
Inspect the connector for oil, corrosion, and loose terminals.
tests.expected: Supply or reference and ground within the OEM specification, signal wire intact, connector clean.

outcomes.label: Circuits and connector good
outcomes.interpretation: The circuit is good; the sensor or its mounting is suspect if the signal is faulty.

outcomes.label: Reference or supply low or missing
outcomes.interpretation: Find the component or wire pulling the reference down.

outcomes.label: Open, short, or chafed signal or ground wire
outcomes.interpretation: Repair the wiring and route it away from ignition components.

outcomes.label: Oil or corrosion in the connector
outcomes.interpretation: Clean or repair the connector and replace the sensor or seal that let oil in.

outcomes.label: Could not access the circuit
outcomes.interpretation: No change.

tests.title: Remove and inspect the suspect sensor
tests.purpose: Check the sensor tip, seating, and part number.
procedure: Key off: remove the suspect sensor per the OEM procedure.
Inspect the tip for metal debris, rubbing damage, cracks, and oil intrusion.
Confirm the part number matches the OEM part and that the mounting surface allows the sensor to seat fully.
Reinstall with a new O-ring and tighten to the OEM specification.
tests.expected: Sensor clean, undamaged, the correct part, and fully seated.

outcomes.label: Sensor clean, undamaged, correct, and seated
outcomes.interpretation: Physical sensor problems are not evident.

outcomes.label: Tip rubbed, cracked, or covered in debris
outcomes.interpretation: Replace the sensor and find why it was damaged (target wheel runout, debris source).

outcomes.label: Sensor not fully seated or incorrect part
outcomes.interpretation: Install the correct sensor and seat it fully.

outcomes.label: Sensor not accessible without major disassembly
outcomes.interpretation: No change.

tests.title: Check oil level and condition
tests.purpose: Confirm the phasers and tensioner have adequate, correct oil.
procedure: Engine off on level ground: check the oil level and condition (sludge, fuel smell, metal).
Confirm the oil type and viscosity match the OEM specification.
If the oil light has been on or noise is present, measure oil pressure with a mechanical gauge per the OEM procedure.
tests.expected: Oil at the correct level, of the specified viscosity, and clean.

outcomes.label: Oil level and condition good
outcomes.interpretation: Oil supply is unlikely to be the cause.

outcomes.label: Oil low, sludged, or wrong viscosity
outcomes.interpretation: Correct the oil level and condition, then recheck; poor oil maintenance also accelerates chain wear.

outcomes.label: Could not check
outcomes.interpretation: No change.

tests.title: Verify cam phaser park position
tests.purpose: Check whether a phaser is returning to its locked park position at idle.
procedure: At warm idle with VVT not commanded, read actual cam position or deviation for each camshaft.
Command the phaser with the scan tool (where supported) and confirm it moves and returns to park.
Listen for start-up clatter, which suggests a lock pin that is not engaging.
tests.expected: Each camshaft at its park position at idle and returning to park after a commanded move.

outcomes.label: Phaser returns to park
outcomes.interpretation: The phaser is not holding the cam out of position.

outcomes.label: Phaser does not return to park or drifts
outcomes.interpretation: Follow the VVT diagnosis: oil supply, solenoid, then phaser.

outcomes.label: Scan tool cannot command or read the phaser
outcomes.interpretation: No change.

tests.title: Verify mechanical timing and chain stretch
tests.purpose: Confirm timing marks and chain wear directly when data points to a mechanical fault.
procedure: Engine cool. Follow the OEM procedure to access the timing marks (this may require removing covers or the valve cover).
Rotate the engine by hand in the normal direction of rotation to the specified position; never rotate a jumped engine forcibly.
Check that all timing marks align and measure chain stretch or tensioner extension per the OEM method.
Inspect guides and the tensioner for wear or breakage.
tests.expected: All marks align and chain stretch or tensioner extension within the OEM specification.

outcomes.label: Timing marks align and chain within specification
outcomes.interpretation: Mechanical timing is correct; a shifted target wheel remains possible.

outcomes.label: Chain stretched, tensioner overextended, or guides worn
outcomes.interpretation: Replace the timing components per the OEM procedure and address the oil maintenance cause.

outcomes.label: Timing out by one or more teeth
outcomes.interpretation: Find why it jumped (tensioner, belt, guide failure) and check for valve damage before re-timing.

outcomes.label: Disassembly deferred pending customer approval
outcomes.interpretation: No change.

tests.title: Inspect the target wheel through the sensor opening
tests.purpose: Look for damaged, missing, or loose teeth on the crank or cam target wheel.
procedure: Key off: remove the sensor and view the target wheel with a borescope or mirror.
Rotate the engine slowly by hand and inspect every tooth for damage, debris, or looseness.
Check whether the wheel is secured correctly to its crank, balancer, or camshaft.
tests.expected: All teeth intact, clean, and the wheel securely located.

outcomes.label: Target wheel intact and secure
outcomes.interpretation: The target wheel is not the cause.

outcomes.label: Damaged, missing, or loose teeth, or wheel shifted
outcomes.interpretation: Repair per the OEM procedure; a shifted balancer or wheel may need replacement.

outcomes.label: Target wheel could not be viewed
outcomes.interpretation: No change.

tests.title: Check technical service bulletins and PCM software level
tests.purpose: Identify known pattern failures, revised parts, or calibration updates for crank and cam sensor and correlation monitors.
procedure: Search OEM service information for bulletins, campaigns, and recalls that match the codes and symptoms for this vehicle.
Read the current PCM calibration ID with a scan tool and compare it with the latest available calibration.
Note any bulletin-directed diagnostic steps or revised parts before continuing.
tools: Scan tool with calibration ID readout
tests.expected: No applicable bulletin and the PCM calibration is current.

outcomes.label: No applicable bulletin; calibration current
outcomes.interpretation: Software and known pattern failures are unlikely; continue with testing.

outcomes.label: Applicable bulletin or calibration update found
outcomes.interpretation: Follow the bulletin procedure, then verify the repair before replacing other parts.

outcomes.label: Service information not available
outcomes.interpretation: No change; continue with direct testing.

verification: Clear codes after recording the freeze frame.
Confirm crank and cam signals are clean and correctly related at idle and under load.
Confirm cam position deviation PIDs are within the OEM specification at park and when commanded.
Complete several cold starts and a drive cycle and confirm no codes return.

playbooks.title: Variable valve timing (cam phasing) faults
playbooks.summary: Camshaft actuator codes are either circuit faults (the solenoid is not being controlled) or performance faults (the cam does not reach the commanded position, P0011/P0014/P0021/P0024 and related). Oil is the first thing to check: low level, sludge, or the wrong viscosity cause many performance codes. Then command-test the solenoid, bench test it and inspect its screen, and check the base cam-to-crank relationship. A stretched or jumped chain produces offsets that phasing cannot correct. Verify mechanical timing before replacing phasers or chains.
clarifyingQuestions: Which camshaft and bank are affected, and is it a circuit or performance code?
When was the oil last changed, and with what viscosity?
Is the oil level correct and has the oil light come on?
Is there a start-up clatter or chain rattle?
Are cam/crank correlation codes (P0016-P0019) also present?

causes.title: Sticking or failed VVT oil control solenoid
causes.description: A spool valve that sticks from debris or wear cannot direct oil to the phaser, so actual cam position does not follow the command.

causes.title: VVT solenoid control circuit fault
causes.description: An open or shorted solenoid winding, wiring, or connector sets a circuit code and disables cam phasing.

causes.title: Restricted VVT oil screen or oil passage
causes.description: Sludge or debris blocks the small screen feeding the solenoid, starving the phaser of oil.

modifiers.match: sludge|oil change overdue|extended oil change|dirty oil

causes.title: Worn or sticking cam phaser
causes.description: Internal wear, a broken lock pin, or leaking seals keep the phaser from holding or reaching the commanded angle.

modifiers.match: knock at start|clatter|rattle (for a few seconds|at start)

causes.title: Low oil level or low oil pressure
causes.description: Cam phasing depends on oil pressure; low oil level or pressure prevents the phaser from moving correctly.

causes.title: Incorrect oil viscosity or specification
causes.description: Oil that is too thick or too thin changes phaser response and sets performance codes.

modifiers.match: oil change|quick lube|wrong oil|heavy oil|thick oil

causes.title: Stretched timing chain or worn guides and tensioner
causes.description: Chain wear shifts the cam relative to the crank so the phaser cannot reach the expected position.

causes.title: Timing chain or belt jumped a tooth
causes.description: A jumped chain leaves the cam out of phase by a fixed amount beyond the phaser's range.

causes.title: Camshaft position sensor signal fault
causes.description: A distorted cam signal makes the PCM calculate the wrong cam angle.

causes.title: PCM calibration requiring an update
causes.description: Some cam timing monitors have been revised by calibration updates.

tests.title: Review codes and desired versus actual cam position
tests.purpose: Separate circuit faults from phasing performance faults, and see which camshaft and bank are affected.
procedure: Record all codes and freeze frames.
At warm idle and during a steady elevated-speed test, graph desired and actual cam position for each camshaft.
Note whether actual lags, overshoots, or does not move, and whether the cam is out of position at park.
Record oil temperature, since phaser response changes with oil temperature.
tests.expected: Actual cam position follows desired closely at all speeds (tolerance per OEM specification).

outcomes.label: Circuit code; solenoid not being controlled
outcomes.interpretation: Test the solenoid and its circuit.

outcomes.label: Actual lags or does not follow desired
outcomes.interpretation: Check oil level and condition, then command-test the solenoid.

outcomes.label: Cam out of position even at park
outcomes.interpretation: Verify cam/crank correlation and mechanical timing.

outcomes.label: Fault not present during the test
outcomes.interpretation: No change; test at the freeze frame oil temperature.

tests.title: Check oil level, condition, and specification
tests.purpose: Confirm the phasing system has adequate, clean oil of the specified grade.
procedure: Engine off on level ground: check the oil level.
Inspect the oil for sludge, fuel dilution, coolant, and metal particles; look under the oil fill cap for sludge.
Confirm the oil viscosity and specification from service records against the OEM requirement.
If the oil light has been on, measure oil pressure with a mechanical gauge per the OEM procedure.
tests.expected: Oil at the correct level, clean, and of the specified viscosity.

outcomes.label: Oil level, condition, and grade correct
outcomes.interpretation: Oil supply is unlikely to be the cause.

outcomes.label: Oil level or pressure low
outcomes.interpretation: Correct the level, find the loss, and recheck phasing.

outcomes.label: Oil sludged or very dirty
outcomes.interpretation: Inspect the solenoid screen; a sludged engine may need further cleaning per OEM guidance.

outcomes.label: Incorrect viscosity or specification
outcomes.interpretation: Change to the specified oil and filter, then recheck phasing.

outcomes.label: Oil specification unknown
outcomes.interpretation: No change; consider an oil change with the specified grade.

tests.title: Command the VVT solenoid and observe cam response
tests.purpose: Check whether the phaser moves when the solenoid is commanded.
procedure: At warm idle, use bidirectional controls to command the cam position or solenoid duty cycle.
Watch actual cam position; commanding advance or retard at idle normally makes the idle rough or stumble as timing changes.
Return to normal control and confirm the cam returns to park.
Repeat for each camshaft.
tests.expected: Actual cam position follows the command promptly and returns to park.

outcomes.label: Cam follows the command and returns to park
outcomes.interpretation: Phasing hardware works at idle; review oil temperature and conditions when the code set.

outcomes.label: Cam does not move or moves slowly
outcomes.interpretation: Bench test the solenoid and inspect its screen before condemning the phaser.

outcomes.label: Cam moves but does not return to park or drifts
outcomes.interpretation: A sticking solenoid or a phaser lock pin problem.

outcomes.label: Scan tool cannot command VVT
outcomes.interpretation: No change.

tests.title: Test the VVT solenoid winding and control circuit
tests.purpose: Confirm the solenoid winding and wiring are intact and the PCM controls it.
procedure: Key off: unplug the solenoid and measure winding resistance, comparing with the OEM specification.
Check wiring continuity to the PCM and for shorts to ground or voltage.
Reconnect and scope the control signal while commanding the solenoid.
Inspect the connector for oil and corrosion.
tests.expected: Winding resistance within specification, wiring intact, and a control signal that follows the command.

outcomes.label: Winding and circuit good
outcomes.interpretation: The electrical side is good; a mechanical solenoid fault is still possible.

outcomes.label: Solenoid winding open or shorted
outcomes.interpretation: Replace the solenoid after confirming the wiring is good.

outcomes.label: Wiring or connector fault, or no control signal
outcomes.interpretation: Repair the wiring or connector; check PCM powers and grounds if no control is present.

outcomes.label: Could not access the solenoid
outcomes.interpretation: No change.

tests.title: Remove, inspect, and bench test the solenoid
tests.purpose: Check the solenoid spool and screen for sticking or debris.
procedure: Key off: remove the solenoid per the OEM procedure.
Inspect the inlet screen and spool for sludge, metal debris, and damage.
Energize briefly per the OEM procedure (fused leads) and watch for smooth spool movement and return.
If debris is present, find the source before reinstalling or replacing.
tests.expected: Screen clean and spool moves smoothly and returns when energized and released.

outcomes.label: Screen clean and spool moves freely
outcomes.interpretation: The solenoid works; focus on the phaser, oil supply, or timing.

outcomes.label: Spool sticks or moves sluggishly
outcomes.interpretation: Replace the solenoid and change the oil if debris is present.

outcomes.label: Screen or passage blocked with sludge or debris
outcomes.interpretation: Clean or replace the screen, change the oil, and investigate the debris source.

outcomes.label: Solenoid not accessible
outcomes.interpretation: No change.

tests.title: Scope cam and crank signals at park
tests.purpose: Check the base cam-to-crank relationship and the cam sensor signal quality.
procedure: At idle with phasing at park, scope the crank and cam signals together.
Compare the cam edge positions with a known-good pattern for this engine.
Check the cam signal for clean edges, correct amplitude, and no dropouts.
tools: Lab scope with at least two channels
tests.expected: Clean cam signal with the base relationship matching the known-good pattern.

outcomes.label: Relationship matches and signal clean
outcomes.interpretation: Base timing and the cam sensor are correct.

outcomes.label: Relationship shifted from known-good
outcomes.interpretation: Verify mechanical timing before replacing phasing components.

outcomes.label: Cam signal distorted or dropping out
outcomes.interpretation: Test the cam sensor circuit and sensor.

outcomes.label: No known-good pattern available
outcomes.interpretation: No change.

tests.title: Verify mechanical timing and chain condition
tests.purpose: Confirm chain stretch or jumped timing directly when data points to a base timing error.
procedure: Engine cool. Follow the OEM procedure to access the timing marks.
Rotate the engine by hand in the normal direction to the specified position; do not force it.
Check that timing marks align and measure chain stretch or tensioner extension per the OEM method.
Inspect guides, tensioner, and phasers for wear or damage.
tests.expected: All marks align and chain stretch within the OEM specification.

outcomes.label: Marks align and chain within specification
outcomes.interpretation: Base timing is correct.

outcomes.label: Chain stretched or guides and tensioner worn
outcomes.interpretation: Replace the timing components per the OEM procedure; inspect phasers at the same time.

outcomes.label: Timing out by one or more teeth
outcomes.interpretation: Find the cause and check for valve damage before re-timing.

outcomes.label: Timing correct but phaser worn, loose, or lock pin damaged
outcomes.interpretation: Replace the phaser per the OEM procedure.

outcomes.label: Disassembly deferred
outcomes.interpretation: No change.

tests.title: Check technical service bulletins and PCM software level
tests.purpose: Identify known pattern failures, revised parts, or calibration updates for variable valve timing.
procedure: Search OEM service information for bulletins, campaigns, and recalls that match the codes and symptoms for this vehicle.
Read the current PCM calibration ID with a scan tool and compare it with the latest available calibration.
Note any bulletin-directed diagnostic steps or revised parts before continuing.
tools: Scan tool with calibration ID readout
tests.expected: No applicable bulletin and the PCM calibration is current.

outcomes.label: No applicable bulletin; calibration current
outcomes.interpretation: Software and known pattern failures are unlikely; continue with testing.

outcomes.label: Applicable bulletin or calibration update found
outcomes.interpretation: Follow the bulletin procedure, then verify the repair before replacing other parts.

outcomes.label: Service information not available
outcomes.interpretation: No change; continue with direct testing.

verification: Clear codes after recording the freeze frame.
Confirm actual cam position follows desired at idle and during a road test, cold and hot.
Confirm no start-up clatter and no correlation codes.
Complete a drive cycle and confirm no camshaft timing codes return.

playbooks.title: Knock sensor circuit and knock detection
playbooks.summary: Knock sensor codes can mean a circuit fault (open, short, or contaminated wiring and connectors, which often sit under the intake), a sensor or mounting problem, or real or false knock. Knock retard data and a road test for audible pinging separate these: circuit codes with no knock activity point to the sensor circuit; retard with pinging points to fuel, EGR, deposits, or overheating; retard without pinging points to mechanical noise or a poorly mounted sensor. Test wiring and output before replacing a sensor, and install sensors at the OEM torque.
clarifyingQuestions: Is there audible pinging under load, and with what fuel grade?
Has the intake manifold or knock sensor been removed or replaced recently?
Are there coolant or oil leaks near the sensor connector?
Is there a mechanical noise, rattle, or loose heat shield?
Are there EGR, lean, or overheating codes as well?

causes.title: Failed knock sensor
causes.description: A cracked or internally failed piezoelectric sensor produces little or no signal, or an erratic one.

causes.title: Knock sensor wiring or connector fault
causes.description: Knock sensor harnesses under the intake are prone to chafing, corrosion, and coolant or oil contamination, causing low/high or intermittent circuit codes.

causes.title: Knock sensor loose, over-torqued, or poorly seated
causes.description: The sensor must be clamped to a clean surface at the specified torque; otherwise its output changes and range/performance codes set.

causes.title: Fuel octane below requirement or poor-quality fuel
causes.description: Fuel with insufficient knock resistance causes real detonation, heavy knock retard, and reduced power.

causes.title: Combustion chamber carbon deposits
causes.description: Carbon raises compression and forms hot spots, causing real detonation, especially on high-mileage or short-trip engines.

causes.title: Insufficient EGR flow (clogged passages)
causes.description: Without the cooling effect of EGR at cruise, combustion temperatures rise and knock increases.

causes.title: Mechanical engine noise detected as knock
causes.description: Loud valve train, piston slap, or bearing noise can be picked up by the knock sensor and interpreted as knock.

causes.title: Loose heat shield, bracket, or accessory noise
causes.description: A loose heat shield, bracket, or failing accessory bearing transmits vibration to the block that the sensor reads as knock.

causes.title: PCM knock input fault
causes.description: An internal PCM fault in the knock processing circuit; confirm only after the sensor and wiring test good.

causes.title: PCM calibration requiring an update
causes.description: Knock detection calibrations have been revised on some vehicles to reduce false detection.

tests.title: Review codes and knock retard data
tests.purpose: Separate knock sensor circuit faults from real or false knock detection.
procedure: Record all codes and freeze frames.
Graph knock retard (or knock count) for each cylinder or sensor at idle, cruise, and moderate acceleration where safe.
Listen for audible pinging during acceleration under load.
Note whether retard appears only with audible ping, all the time, or not at all.
tests.expected: Little or no knock retard under normal load and no audible pinging.

outcomes.label: Circuit code with no knock activity (default retard)
outcomes.interpretation: Test the sensor circuit and sensor output.

outcomes.label: Knock retard with audible pinging under load
outcomes.interpretation: Real detonation: check fuel, EGR flow, and deposits; also rule out lean or overheating conditions.

outcomes.label: Knock retard or range code without audible pinging
outcomes.interpretation: Possible false knock: listen for mechanical noise and check sensor mounting.

outcomes.label: No activity or codes during the test
outcomes.interpretation: No change.

tests.title: Test the knock sensor circuit and connector
tests.purpose: Find wiring, shielding, or connector faults.
procedure: Key off: locate the knock sensor connector (often under the intake manifold) and inspect for oil, coolant, corrosion, and chafing.
Measure sensor resistance or bias voltage as specified by the OEM (some sensors use a bias voltage from the PCM).
Check continuity of the signal and return circuits to the PCM and check for shorts to ground, voltage, and the shield.
Wiggle the harness while monitoring knock data or voltage.
tests.expected: Circuit values within the OEM specification, no opens or shorts, and a clean connector.

outcomes.label: Wiring and connector good
outcomes.interpretation: The circuit is good; check sensor output and mounting.

outcomes.label: Open, short, chafe, or contaminated connector found
outcomes.interpretation: Repair the wiring or connector and correct any fluid leak that contaminated it.

outcomes.label: Wiring good, but the sensor's resistance or bias reading is out of specification
outcomes.interpretation: The sensor is likely faulty; inspect its mounting when replacing it.

outcomes.label: Connector not accessible without removing the intake
outcomes.interpretation: No change.

tests.title: Scope knock sensor output
tests.purpose: Confirm the sensor produces a signal in response to vibration.
procedure: Back-probe the knock sensor signal with a lab scope.
With the engine off, lightly tap the block near the sensor with a small tool and watch for a signal.
With the engine running, compare the sensor output at idle and during a snap throttle, and compare with a second sensor if fitted.
tests.expected: A clear signal when tapped and increasing activity with engine speed.

outcomes.label: Sensor responds clearly
outcomes.interpretation: The sensor produces a signal.

outcomes.label: No or weak signal when tapped
outcomes.interpretation: Check sensor mounting and the circuit; replace the sensor if they are good.

outcomes.label: Could not access the signal wire
outcomes.interpretation: No change.

tests.title: Inspect knock sensor mounting
tests.purpose: Confirm the sensor is clean, undamaged, and tightened to specification.
procedure: Gain access per the OEM procedure (intake removal may be needed).
Check the sensor for cracks and the mounting surface for corrosion, paint, or debris.
Confirm fastener type and torque against the OEM specification; do not add washers or thread sealant unless specified.
Reinstall with the specified torque.
tests.expected: Sensor intact, clean mounting surface, and correct fastener torque.

outcomes.label: Sensor and mounting correct
outcomes.interpretation: Mounting is not the cause.

outcomes.label: Loose, over-torqued, or corroded mounting
outcomes.interpretation: Clean the surface and install at the specified torque, then retest.

outcomes.label: Sensor body cracked or damaged
outcomes.interpretation: Replace the sensor and install at the specified torque.

outcomes.label: Access deferred
outcomes.interpretation: No change.

tests.title: Check fuel grade and quality
tests.purpose: Rule out low-octane or poor-quality fuel as a source of real knock.
procedure: Confirm the OEM fuel octane requirement (fuel door or owner information).
Ask where and what grade the customer last refueled.
Take a fuel sample if quality is suspect, with fire precautions in place.
If practical, refill with the recommended grade and recheck knock retard.
tests.expected: Fuel of the recommended grade and quality in use.

outcomes.label: Correct fuel grade in use
outcomes.interpretation: Fuel is unlikely to be the cause.

outcomes.label: Lower grade than required, or knock drops after refueling with the correct grade
outcomes.interpretation: Use the recommended fuel and recheck.

outcomes.label: Fuel history unknown
outcomes.interpretation: No change.

tests.title: Listen for mechanical noises the sensor may detect
tests.purpose: Identify real mechanical noise that could be misread as knock.
procedure: With the engine running, use a stethoscope to listen at the valve covers, block near the sensor, accessories, and exhaust heat shields.
Tap heat shields and brackets with the engine off to find loose parts.
Remove the accessory belt briefly (engine off; run only for a short time if the OEM permits) to isolate accessory bearing noise.
Keep hands, hair, and tools clear of the belt and fan.
tests.expected: No abnormal mechanical noise or loose parts.

outcomes.label: No abnormal noise found
outcomes.interpretation: Mechanical noise is not the cause.

outcomes.label: Valve train or internal engine noise found
outcomes.interpretation: Diagnose the engine noise; the knock code may be a symptom.

outcomes.label: Loose heat shield, bracket, or noisy accessory found
outcomes.interpretation: Repair the loose part or accessory and recheck knock data.

outcomes.label: Noise could not be isolated
outcomes.interpretation: No change.

tests.title: Borescope the combustion chambers for carbon
tests.purpose: Confirm heavy combustion chamber deposits before recommending cleaning.
procedure: Engine cool. Remove spark plugs and inspect piston tops and chambers with a borescope.
Compare deposit thickness between cylinders.
Reinstall plugs tightened to the OEM specification.
tests.expected: Light, even deposits only.

outcomes.label: Light deposits
outcomes.interpretation: Deposits are not the cause.

outcomes.label: Heavy carbon deposits
outcomes.interpretation: Clean using an OEM-approved method and address the cause (oil consumption, short trips).

outcomes.label: Plugs not accessible
outcomes.interpretation: No change.

tests.title: Check EGR flow at cruise
tests.purpose: Confirm EGR is flowing enough to control combustion temperature.
procedure: During a steady cruise, graph commanded and actual EGR (position, flow, or pressure feedback PIDs).
Observe MAP or fuel trim changes when EGR is commanded, where the OEM provides a test.
If flow is low, inspect passages per the EGR diagnosis.
tests.expected: EGR flow follows the command at cruise (per OEM specification).

outcomes.label: EGR flows as commanded
outcomes.interpretation: EGR flow is not the cause.

outcomes.label: EGR flow low or absent
outcomes.interpretation: Diagnose the EGR system and clean the passages.

outcomes.label: Engine has no external EGR
outcomes.interpretation: Not applicable.

tests.title: Check technical service bulletins and PCM software level
tests.purpose: Identify known pattern failures, revised parts, or calibration updates for knock sensing.
procedure: Search OEM service information for bulletins, campaigns, and recalls that match the codes and symptoms for this vehicle.
Read the current PCM calibration ID with a scan tool and compare it with the latest available calibration.
Note any bulletin-directed diagnostic steps or revised parts before continuing.
tools: Scan tool with calibration ID readout
tests.expected: No applicable bulletin and the PCM calibration is current.

outcomes.label: No applicable bulletin; calibration current
outcomes.interpretation: Software and known pattern failures are unlikely; continue with testing.

outcomes.label: Applicable bulletin or calibration update found
outcomes.interpretation: Follow the bulletin procedure, then verify the repair before replacing other parts.

outcomes.label: Service information not available
outcomes.interpretation: No change; continue with direct testing.

verification: Clear codes after recording the freeze frame.
Road test under moderate load and confirm knock retard is minimal and no pinging is heard.
Confirm knock sensor data is active and plausible.
Complete a drive cycle and confirm no knock sensor codes return.

playbooks.title: Oil pressure warning and engine noise
playbooks.summary: An oil pressure warning or code must be treated as urgent until actual pressure is verified with a mechanical gauge. If the gauge shows normal pressure, the sensor or its circuit is at fault. If pressure is truly low, check the oil level and grade first, then the filter, pickup, pump, and bearings. Ticking, rattling, and knocking noises are located by sound and by when they occur: top-end ticks (valve train or low oil), manifold ticks that fade when warm (exhaust leak), start-up rattles (timing chain), and deep knocks under load (bearings).
