Stop running the engine if pressure is confirmed low.
clarifyingQuestions: Is the oil pressure light or gauge warning on steadily, flickering at idle, or only on the scan tool?
What is the oil level, and when was the oil last changed and with what grade and filter?
Is the noise a tick, rattle, or deep knock, and where does it seem to come from?
Is it worse cold or hot, at start-up, or under load?
Has the engine run low on oil or overheated recently?

causes.title: Low oil level
causes.description: Too little oil lets the pickup draw air under braking, cornering, or acceleration, dropping pressure and causing lifter tick and bearing noise.

modifiers.reason: Oil light or oil loss reported

causes.title: Incorrect oil viscosity or degraded oil
causes.description: Oil that is too thin, fuel-diluted, or overdue for change lowers hot oil pressure and quiets hydraulic lifters poorly.

causes.title: Failed oil pressure sensor or switch
causes.description: A leaking or failed sender gives a false low or erratic reading while actual pressure is normal.

modifiers.reason: Oil pressure sensor circuit or range code

causes.title: Oil pressure sensor wiring or connector fault
causes.description: An open, shorted, or oil-soaked connector or wire sets circuit codes and false warnings.

causes.title: Restricted oil pickup screen
causes.description: Sludge or gasket material on the pickup screen restricts flow, so pressure drops at higher speeds or when hot.

modifiers.reason: Low pressure at speed or hot

causes.title: Worn or failed oil pump or stuck pressure relief valve
causes.description: Pump wear or a relief valve stuck open lowers pressure at all speeds.

causes.title: Worn crankshaft (rod or main) bearings
causes.description: Excess bearing clearance lowers oil pressure, especially hot at idle, and produces a deep knock that rises with load.

causes.title: Valve train noise (lifter, lash adjuster, rocker, or cam wear)
causes.description: A sticking or collapsed lifter, worn rocker, or excessive lash produces a ticking at half engine speed from the top of the engine.

causes.title: Exhaust manifold leak (ticking noise)
causes.description: A leaking manifold gasket or broken stud ticks like a lifter, loudest cold and quieter as the metal expands.

causes.title: Worn timing chain, guides, or tensioner (rattle)
causes.description: A worn chain or tensioner slaps against guides, causing a rattle from the front of the engine, often at start-up.

causes.title: Incorrect or defective oil filter
causes.description: A filter with the wrong bypass or anti-drainback valve, or a defective filter, lowers pressure or causes start-up noise.

tests.title: Check oil level, condition, and grade
tests.purpose: Rule out the most common and easiest causes first.
procedure: Engine off on level ground, after the oil has drained back: check the oil level.
Inspect oil condition for sludge, fuel smell, coolant (milky), and metal particles.
Confirm the oil viscosity and filter from records or labels against the OEM specification.
Look for external oil leaks, including at the oil pressure sensor.
tests.expected: Oil at the correct level, of the specified grade, clean, and with the correct filter.

outcomes.label: Oil level, condition, and grade correct
outcomes.interpretation: Oil level and grade are not the cause.

outcomes.label: Oil level low
outcomes.interpretation: Top up, find the leak or consumption, and recheck pressure and noise; running low may already have damaged the engine.

outcomes.label: Oil degraded, fuel-diluted, wrong grade, or wrong filter
outcomes.interpretation: Change the oil and filter to the OEM specification and recheck.

outcomes.label: Could not check reliably
outcomes.interpretation: No change.

tests.title: Measure oil pressure with a mechanical gauge
tests.purpose: Determine whether actual oil pressure is low or only the sensor reading is wrong.
procedure: Remove the oil pressure sensor or use the OEM test port and install a mechanical gauge with the correct adapter.
Start the engine and immediately check for pressure and leaks; shut down at once if no pressure is shown.
Record pressure at warm idle and at a specified higher engine speed, and compare with the OEM specification at operating temperature.
Compare the gauge with the oil pressure PID or dash gauge.
tools: Mechanical oil pressure gauge and adapters
tests.expected: Pressure within the OEM specification at idle and elevated speed, matching the PID.

outcomes.label: Gauge normal, but the PID or warning disagrees
outcomes.interpretation: Actual pressure is fine; test the sensor and its circuit.

outcomes.label: Gauge confirms low pressure
outcomes.interpretation: Actual pressure is low: do not continue running the engine; correct the oil, then inspect the pickup, pump, and bearings.

outcomes.label: Gauge normal and the PID agrees
outcomes.interpretation: Oil pressure is normal; locate the noise source.

outcomes.label: Could not connect a gauge
outcomes.interpretation: No change.

tests.title: Test the oil pressure sensor circuit
tests.purpose: Separate a failed sensor from wiring or connector faults.
procedure: Key on, engine off: note the oil pressure PID or warning lamp status.
Unplug the sensor and check the reference or supply, signal, and ground at the harness per the wiring diagram.
For a switch, ground or open the signal wire and confirm the lamp or PID responds.
Inspect the connector for oil intrusion and corrosion.
tests.expected: Circuit values within the OEM specification and the PID or lamp responds to the circuit test.

outcomes.label: Circuit good and responds to the test
outcomes.interpretation: The circuit is good; if the gauge shows normal pressure, the sensor is at fault.

outcomes.label: Open, short, or contaminated connector
outcomes.interpretation: Repair the circuit; oil in the connector usually means the sensor is leaking and must be replaced too.

outcomes.label: Could not access the circuit
outcomes.interpretation: No change.

tests.title: Locate the engine noise
tests.purpose: Find where the noise comes from and how it relates to engine speed, temperature, and load.
procedure: With the engine running, use a stethoscope to compare the valve covers, front timing cover, exhaust manifolds, lower block, and accessories.
Note whether the noise is at camshaft speed (half engine speed) or crankshaft speed, and whether it changes with temperature or load.
Keep hands, clothing, and tools clear of belts and fans, and avoid hot exhaust components.
tests.expected: No abnormal mechanical noise.

outcomes.label: Ticking from the valve cover area at camshaft speed
outcomes.interpretation: Check oil supply first, then diagnose the valve train.

outcomes.label: Ticking at the exhaust manifold, loudest cold
outcomes.interpretation: Inspect the manifold and studs for an exhaust leak.

outcomes.label: Rattle from the front timing cover, often at start-up
outcomes.interpretation: Check cam/crank correlation and chain condition.

outcomes.label: Deep knock from the lower engine, louder under load
outcomes.interpretation: Suspect bearing wear; limit engine running and confirm with a cylinder kill test and oil inspection.

outcomes.label: No abnormal noise heard
outcomes.interpretation: No change; oil pressure faults may be electrical.

tests.title: Disable cylinders one at a time while listening to the knock
tests.purpose: Confirm a rod bearing knock by seeing whether it changes when a cylinder is disabled.
procedure: Use the scan tool power balance or injector disable function (or unplug one coil at a time, with the engine running only briefly).
Listen to the knock as each cylinder is disabled.
Restore all cylinders and clear any codes set by the test.
tools: Scan tool with cylinder disable function
tests.expected: No knock present, or the noise does not change with any cylinder disabled.

outcomes.label: Knock unchanged with any cylinder disabled
outcomes.interpretation: A rod bearing knock is less likely; main bearings or other sources remain possible.

outcomes.label: Knock quiets or changes when one cylinder is disabled
outcomes.interpretation: Strongly suggests a rod bearing fault on that cylinder; plan engine repair.

outcomes.label: No knock to evaluate
outcomes.interpretation: No change.

tests.title: Inspect the exhaust manifold for leaks
tests.purpose: Confirm an exhaust leak that sounds like a tick.
procedure: Cold engine: start it and listen at the manifold flange and joints with a stethoscope or length of hose.
Engine off and cool: look for soot trails, cracked manifolds, and broken or missing studs.
Optionally introduce low-pressure smoke into the tailpipe with the engine off.
tests.expected: No exhaust leaks at the manifold or joints.

outcomes.label: No leak found
outcomes.interpretation: The exhaust is not the noise source.

outcomes.label: Leak, soot trail, or broken stud found
outcomes.interpretation: Repair the manifold gasket or studs and recheck the noise.

outcomes.label: Could not inspect the full manifold
outcomes.interpretation: No change.

tests.title: Drain oil and inspect the filter for debris
tests.purpose: Look for bearing material or metal that indicates internal wear.
procedure: Drain the oil into a clean pan and look for metal particles or sludge.
Cut open the oil filter with a filter cutter and inspect the element for metal, bearing material, and gasket debris.
Confirm the filter is the correct part for the engine.
Refill with the specified oil and a correct filter.
tests.expected: No significant metal or debris and the correct filter installed.

outcomes.label: No significant debris; correct filter
outcomes.interpretation: Major internal wear is less likely.

outcomes.label: Bearing material or significant metal found
outcomes.interpretation: Internal engine damage is likely; inspect the bearings before further running.

outcomes.label: Sludge or gasket sealant debris found
outcomes.interpretation: Inspect the pickup screen for restriction.

outcomes.label: Incorrect or defective filter
outcomes.interpretation: Install the correct filter and recheck pressure and noise.

outcomes.label: Not performed
outcomes.interpretation: No change.

tests.title: Remove the oil pan and inspect the pickup, pump, and bearings
tests.purpose: Confirm the cause of verified low oil pressure.
procedure: Support the vehicle securely on a lift or jack stands.
Remove the oil pan per the OEM procedure.
Inspect the pickup screen and tube O-ring for restriction or leaks, and inspect the pump and relief valve where accessible.
Inspect or measure rod and main bearing clearances per the OEM procedure where practical.
Reinstall with new gaskets and the specified sealant and torque.
tests.expected: Clean pickup, sealed pickup tube, functioning pump and relief valve, and bearing clearances within the OEM specification.

outcomes.label: Pickup, pump, and bearings in specification
outcomes.interpretation: Look elsewhere for low pressure (sensor, filter, oil grade).

outcomes.label: Pickup screen restricted or tube O-ring leaking
outcomes.interpretation: Clean or replace the pickup and O-ring and find the debris source.

outcomes.label: Pump worn or relief valve stuck
outcomes.interpretation: Replace the pump or relief valve and check for debris.

outcomes.label: Bearing clearance excessive or bearings damaged
outcomes.interpretation: Plan engine repair; confirm the crankshaft condition.

outcomes.label: Inspection deferred pending approval
outcomes.interpretation: No change.

tests.title: Check timing chain condition
tests.purpose: Confirm a worn chain or tensioner as the source of a front-end rattle.
procedure: Review cam/crank correlation or cam position deviation PIDs at idle with phasers at park.
Listen at the timing cover at start-up after the engine has sat.
Where the OEM provides a method, measure chain stretch or tensioner extension through an inspection port or after removing the valve cover.
tests.expected: Correlation within specification and no chain rattle.

outcomes.label: Chain and tensioner within specification
outcomes.interpretation: The timing chain is not the noise source.

outcomes.label: Correlation out or chain and tensioner worn
outcomes.interpretation: Replace timing components per the OEM procedure and correct the oil maintenance cause.

outcomes.label: Chain not inspected
outcomes.interpretation: No change.

verification: Confirm oil pressure with a mechanical gauge is within the OEM specification at idle and elevated speed, hot.
Confirm the oil pressure PID and warning lamp agree with the gauge.
Confirm the reported noise is gone or identified as normal for the engine.
Recheck oil level after a road test and clear codes; confirm none return.

playbooks.title: Low power without codes (restricted exhaust, compression, timing)
playbooks.summary: When an engine feels down on power with no codes, start with a road test and wide-open-throttle data to decide whether the engine is not breathing (exhaust or intake restriction, retarded or jumped valve timing, low compression), not getting full throttle, not getting enough fuel at high load, or whether the loss is outside the engine (dragging brakes or a slipping torque converter stator). A vacuum gauge and back-pressure test confirm an exhaust restriction; a plugged converter usually has a root cause such as misfire or oil consumption that must be fixed too. For turbocharged underboost, use the turbo/boost playbook instead.
clarifyingQuestions: Is the loss worse from a stop, at highway speed, or climbing hills?
Did it start suddenly or gradually?
Are there any codes, including history, and has the MIL ever flashed?
Is there a rattle underneath, a sulfur smell, or a glowing converter?
Does the vehicle coast freely, and is any wheel hotter than the others?

causes.title: Exhaust restriction (plugged converter, collapsed muffler, or crushed pipe)
causes.description: A restricted exhaust traps exhaust gas in the cylinders; power falls off progressively with speed and load, often with a hot converter or rattle.

modifiers.match: gets worse|falls off|top end|highway|won.?t go (over|past)|max(imum)? speed

modifiers.reason: Hot or rattling converter or sulfur odor

causes.title: Low compression on several cylinders
causes.description: General wear or valve sealing problems lower cylinder pressure and power across the rev range.

causes.title: Retarded cam timing from a stretched chain
causes.description: Retarded valve timing lowers cylinder filling and low-speed torque.

causes.title: Timing belt or chain jumped a tooth
causes.description: A jumped belt or chain causes a sudden, large loss of power and often poor idle and starting.

causes.title: Restricted air filter or inlet
causes.description: A plugged filter or blocked inlet limits airflow at high load, reducing maximum power.

causes.title: Throttle not reaching full opening
causes.description: A throttle body or pedal assembly that does not reach full travel (or an obstruction such as a floor mat) limits airflow.

causes.title: Dragging brakes
causes.description: A sticking caliper or parking brake adds load, making the vehicle feel down on power and coast poorly.

modifiers.match: drag|pull|brake smell|hot wheel|burning smell|coasts poorly|parking brake

causes.title: Torque converter stator clutch slipping
causes.description: A slipping stator one-way clutch removes torque multiplication, so acceleration from a stop is very poor while cruising is normal.

causes.title: Skewed MAP sensor (speed-density engines)
causes.description: A MAP reading lower than actual reduces calculated load and fueling on engines that rely on MAP.

causes.title: Large vacuum leak
causes.description: A large leak disturbs fueling and idle; it more commonly causes lean running than low power but can reduce responsiveness.

causes.title: Low fuel pressure or volume under load
causes.description: Fuel supply that falls off at high demand leans the engine and cuts power at high load.

modifiers.reason: Lean or low fuel pressure history

tests.title: Road test to characterize the power loss
tests.purpose: Determine when the power loss occurs so the likely system can be targeted.
procedure: Confirm there are no stored, pending, or history codes and that no reduced-power mode is active.
In a safe, legal location, compare acceleration from a stop, passing acceleration at speed, and sustained climbing.
Note whether power fades the longer the vehicle is driven, and whether the vehicle coasts freely.
Check wheel temperatures by careful observation afterward (without touching hot parts).
tests.expected: Acceleration normal for the vehicle in all conditions and the vehicle coasts freely.

outcomes.label: Weak only from a stop; normal once moving
outcomes.interpretation: Suspect the torque converter or low-speed torque issues.

outcomes.label: Power falls off with speed or sustained load
outcomes.interpretation: Check exhaust restriction, intake restriction, and fuel supply under load.

outcomes.label: Weak in all conditions
outcomes.interpretation: Check throttle opening, valve timing, compression, and sensor plausibility.

outcomes.label: Coasts poorly or a wheel is noticeably hotter
outcomes.interpretation: Inspect the brakes for drag before any engine testing.

outcomes.label: Power loss not reproduced
outcomes.interpretation: No change.

tests.title: Record wide-open-throttle data
tests.purpose: Check whether the engine is getting full throttle, full airflow, and enough fuel.
procedure: In a safe, legal location, record a wide-open-throttle acceleration with the scan tool (a helper should operate the scan tool).
Record throttle position (actual and desired), pedal position, MAF or calculated load, rpm, spark timing, knock retard, and fuel trims or lambda.
Compare peak airflow with expected values for the engine (per OEM specification or known-good data).
tools: Scan tool with graphing and recording
tests.expected: Full throttle opening, airflow and load as expected, and mixture on target at wide-open throttle.

outcomes.label: Throttle does not reach full opening
outcomes.interpretation: Check pedal travel, floor mats, and the throttle body.

outcomes.label: Full throttle but airflow or load lower than expected
outcomes.interpretation: Check breathing: exhaust back pressure, intake restriction, valve timing, and compression.

outcomes.label: Airflow normal but mixture lean at wide-open throttle
outcomes.interpretation: Test fuel pressure and volume under load.

outcomes.label: Throttle, airflow, and mixture all normal
outcomes.interpretation: The engine is producing expected airflow; look at drivetrain and brake drag.

outcomes.label: Test could not be performed safely
outcomes.interpretation: No change.

tests.title: Compare the MAP PID with a vacuum gauge and barometric pressure
tests.purpose: Verify the MAP sensor reading against an independent gauge and use the vacuum pattern to spot leaks and exhaust restriction.
procedure: Key on, engine off: compare the MAP and BARO PIDs; both should indicate current atmospheric pressure.
Tee a vacuum gauge (or a pressure transducer on a lab scope) into a manifold vacuum source close to the MAP sensor port.
Start the engine and compare gauge vacuum with the MAP PID at warm idle, converting units as needed.
Hold a steady elevated engine speed (for example about 2,500 rpm) for up to a minute and watch whether vacuum stays steady or slowly falls.
Snap the throttle and note how quickly MAP and the gauge respond and recover.
tools: Vacuum gauge or pressure transducer with lab scope
tests.expected: MAP PID matches the gauge and BARO at key-on, idle vacuum is steady, and vacuum holds or rises slightly at a sustained elevated speed (normal values per OEM specification and altitude (general guideline — verify against OEM specification)).

outcomes.label: MAP agrees with the gauge and the vacuum pattern is normal
outcomes.interpretation: MAP sensing and basic engine breathing are normal; focus on other causes.

outcomes.label: MAP PID disagrees with the gauge or with BARO at key-on
outcomes.interpretation: The MAP sensor, its hose, or its circuit is skewed; test the circuit before replacing the sensor.

outcomes.label: MAP and gauge agree, but idle vacuum is low or unsteady
outcomes.interpretation: Suggests an intake leak, retarded valve timing, or a mechanical fault; smoke test the intake and verify timing.

outcomes.label: Vacuum falls steadily at a sustained elevated speed or recovers slowly after a snap
outcomes.interpretation: Classic sign of exhaust restriction; confirm with a back-pressure test.

outcomes.label: No suitable manifold vacuum port available
outcomes.interpretation: No change; use the MAP PID with a pressure transducer or other tests.

tests.title: Measure exhaust back pressure
tests.purpose: Confirm or rule out exhaust restriction directly.
procedure: Engine cool: remove the upstream O2 sensor (or use another OEM-approved port) and install a back-pressure gauge.
Measure back pressure at idle and at a steady elevated engine speed, and during a snap throttle.

Compare with the OEM specification or a general guideline (general guideline: back pressure should stay low at idle and rise only modestly at 2,500 rpm (general guideline — verify against OEM specification)).
If high, move the test point downstream (after the converter) to locate the restriction.
Reinstall the sensor with the correct thread compound only if the OEM specifies it.
tools: Exhaust back-pressure gauge with O2 port adapter
tests.expected: Back pressure within the OEM specification at idle and elevated speed.

outcomes.label: Back pressure within specification
outcomes.interpretation: The exhaust is not restricted.

outcomes.label: Back pressure high
outcomes.interpretation: Locate the restriction and repair it; find the root cause of a failed converter (misfire, rich running, oil or coolant consumption).

outcomes.label: Sensor could not be removed
outcomes.interpretation: No change; use the vacuum or temperature methods instead.

tests.title: Inspect the exhaust system and converter
tests.purpose: Look for physical damage or signs of a plugged converter.
procedure: Raise and support the vehicle securely.
Inspect pipes for crushing or kinks and the muffler for internal rattle or collapse.
Tap the converter with a rubber mallet (engine cool) and listen for loose substrate.
With the engine running, compare converter inlet and outlet temperatures with an infrared thermometer, keeping clear of hot surfaces and rotating parts.
tests.expected: No physical damage, no loose substrate, and normal converter temperatures.

outcomes.label: No damage or abnormal signs
outcomes.interpretation: No visible restriction; a plugged converter is still possible without external signs.

outcomes.label: Crushed pipe, collapsed muffler, loose substrate, or overheated converter
outcomes.interpretation: Confirm with a back-pressure test and repair.

outcomes.label: Could not inspect underneath
outcomes.interpretation: No change.

tests.title: Inspect the air filter and inlet
tests.purpose: Rule out an intake restriction.
procedure: Engine off: remove and inspect the air filter for heavy dirt, water, or debris.
Inspect the inlet snorkel, resonators, and ducts for blockage, nests, or collapse.
Optionally measure intake restriction at wide-open throttle and compare with the OEM specification.
tests.expected: Clean filter and unobstructed inlet.

outcomes.label: Filter and inlet clear
outcomes.interpretation: Intake restriction is not the cause.

outcomes.label: Filter plugged or inlet obstructed
outcomes.interpretation: Replace the filter or clear the obstruction and retest.

outcomes.label: Not inspected
outcomes.interpretation: No change.

tests.title: Verify full pedal and throttle travel
tests.purpose: Confirm the throttle opens fully when the pedal is pressed to the floor.
procedure: Check for floor mats or objects limiting pedal travel.
Key on, engine off: press the pedal fully and watch pedal position and throttle position PIDs; keep fingers out of the throttle bore.
Visually confirm the throttle plate reaches full opening, then release.
Check for throttle bore deposits and binding.
tests.expected: Pedal and throttle PIDs reach their full-travel values (per OEM specification) and the plate opens fully.

outcomes.label: Full travel reached
outcomes.interpretation: Throttle opening is not the cause.

outcomes.label: Pedal or throttle does not reach full travel
outcomes.interpretation: Correct the obstruction or diagnose the pedal and throttle body.

outcomes.label: Not checked
outcomes.interpretation: No change.

tests.title: Relative compression and cam/crank correlation check
tests.purpose: Check for low compression and retarded or jumped valve timing.
procedure: Disable fuel and ignition per the OEM procedure and perform a relative compression test with a lab scope and high-amp probe; confirm low results with a cranking compression test.
Review cam/crank correlation PIDs or scope crank and cam signals together and compare with a known-good pattern.
Restore fuel and ignition and clear any codes set by the test.
tests.expected: Compression even and within the OEM specification, with correct cam/crank correlation.

outcomes.label: Compression and timing correct
outcomes.interpretation: Engine mechanical condition is good.

outcomes.label: Compression low on one or more cylinders; timing correct
outcomes.interpretation: Perform a leak-down test to find the cause.

outcomes.label: Cam/crank correlation retarded or shifted
outcomes.interpretation: Verify mechanical timing and inspect the chain or belt.

outcomes.label: Could not safely perform the test
outcomes.interpretation: No change.

tests.title: Check for brake drag
tests.purpose: Rule out dragging brakes that make the vehicle feel down on power.
procedure: Raise and support the vehicle securely with the transmission in neutral and the parking brake released (wheels chocked as required).
Rotate each wheel by hand and compare resistance.
After a drive, carefully compare wheel and rotor temperatures with an infrared thermometer.
Inspect calipers, slides, and parking brake cables for binding.
tests.expected: All wheels rotate freely with similar temperatures.

outcomes.label: All wheels rotate freely
outcomes.interpretation: Brake drag is not the cause.

outcomes.label: A wheel drags or runs hot
outcomes.interpretation: Repair the caliper, slides, hose, or parking brake; follow the brake playbook.

outcomes.label: Could not lift the vehicle
outcomes.interpretation: No change.

tests.title: Check fuel pressure under load
tests.purpose: Confirm fuel supply keeps up at high demand.
procedure: Connect a fuel pressure gauge (port injection) or monitor low-side and rail pressure PIDs (direct injection) per the OEM procedure.
Record pressure during a loaded road test or wide-open-throttle acceleration with a helper.
Compare actual with desired and with the OEM specification.
Check for leaks at the gauge connection before and after the test.
tests.expected: Fuel pressure within the OEM specification and steady under load.

outcomes.label: Pressure holds under load
outcomes.interpretation: Fuel supply is adequate.

outcomes.label: Pressure falls under load
outcomes.interpretation: Diagnose the fuel supply before other repairs.

outcomes.label: Could not connect a gauge
outcomes.interpretation: No change.

verification: Road test and confirm normal acceleration from a stop, when passing, and when climbing.
Confirm wide-open-throttle airflow and throttle opening are as expected.
Confirm vacuum is steady at idle and at a sustained elevated speed.
Recheck for any pending codes after the road test.
